I hope the platform can listen to the voices of users more and don’t let these beautiful moments just stay in regrets.

As an ordinary working man, I hesitated for a long time to spend a lot of money to watch the Olympic 100m final. I am 28 years old and my income is not high, but I have been dreaming about it for 15 years, so I gritted my teeth and bought the ticket. At that moment, when the music started playing, I burst into tears - not to show off, but to truly feel that it is worth it to pay for what you love. There is equal opportunity in this world, and as long as you are willing to fight for it, you can have your own moment of glory.

The moment I saw the Italian women's volleyball team win the championship, my eyes got wet. As old fans, we have waited too long. From the regrettable final in Atlanta to today's gold medal, everything has come true. This is not only a victory for the team, but also a glory for the entire country. It fills a gap in history and allows every Italian to proudly say: We finally did it!

Some South Africans always feel that they are 'tanned Europeans' and use other African countries as a backdrop. This sense of superiority is really ridiculous. South Africa's economy is strong, with stock markets and shopping malls, but without Nigeria's oil and Zimbabwe's labor, how can it still be so poor? Not to mention the terrible power rationing, the outrageous wealth gap, and the crime rate, which is better than even the slums of Lagos. To put it bluntly, South Africa is like a show-off relative who wears designer shoes but borrows money to go home. Wake up, without the support of the entire Africa, you don’t even have half the confidence!

South Africa's positioning as an 'African country' is a joke! Those who are still advocating to go there, what else do they want besides economic desperation? This is not a real choice at all, but a forced choice. Stop beautifying this kind of immigration motivation. The procedures may seem reasonable, but in fact they cover up deep-seated injustices. Afrophobia? It is nothing more than a fig leaf to cover up the colonial legacy.

Stop fooling people with your false 'South African identity'! Look at these artificial borders that separate the Basotho, Batswana, Swazis, Tsonga, Ndebele, Zulus, and even the nomadic Khoi. This is clearly a hierarchical system carefully designed by the colonizers, which puts Europeans of mixed race at the top while indigenous peoples are marginalized. What unified South African identity are we now expected to believe in? That's ridiculous! My identity first comes from my tribe. This is a fact rooted in blood and history. It cannot be replaced by empty slogans.

Look at this justice system, what a travesty! Chinese companies pollute the environment in Africa, but no one is prosecuted, but South Africa can give fair sentences. Isn't this a blatant double standard? Stop using development as an excuse. Who will bear the cost of environmental damage? It’s time for African countries to wake up and strengthen regulations to protect our homeland instead of letting polluters go unpunished!

My heart clenched when I heard about your aunt's experience. How can medical workers treat patients like this? This is not only a personal experience, but also a microcosm of the xenophobia of the entire society. We must stand up, report these injustices, and make hospitals pay for their discrimination. At the same time, we call for more media attention to promote change. I really hope that one day, everyone in South Africa can put aside their prejudices and treat each other with tolerance. This is not only moral progress, but also our common hope.

This actually reflects the reality of the current labor market: certain technical positions such as fitters are indeed in short supply, and companies have to rely on overseas recruitment to solve the problem. From an economic perspective, this reflects the self-regulation of the market mechanism, and the introduction of talents through the visa system can effectively fill the gap. At the social level, following existing legal procedures ensures compliance with transnational flows and avoids disorderly competition. Overall, this is a pragmatic response strategy rather than a fundamental change.

Isn't Israel just trying to copy South Africa's Bantustan system by annexing Area C? Enclosing Palestinians in Areas A and B to protect them in name is actually a replica of apartheid! Playing the citizenship game in law is still racial discrimination at heart. This strategy is simply digging its own grave. If Israel really takes this path, it will be the biggest strategic mistake in history, and not even a nuclear bomb can save it. Wake up, don’t be fooled by those settler lobbying. This is not about protecting the Jewish state at all, but destroying it with your own hands!

It's really ridiculous. Some people only think that Nigeria is a paradise by comparing it with those war-torn or natural disaster-torn countries. Have you never been to South Africa, Kenya or the Netherlands? The West is not good at everything, but at least it is much better than Nigeria. The fruits of development are unevenly distributed and ordinary people live a difficult life. This kind of comparison standard is simply deceiving itself. Stop fooling people with such low standards. What we need is real progress, not self-comforting illusions.

Seriously, only 1% of people in South Africa can live a middle-class life. This distribution system is absolutely terrible! Stop fooling people with the median salary, that doesn’t define class at all. The reality is that most people cannot even enjoy basic fairness. How can this be procedural justice? It's clearly a blatant injustice.

I've had enough! Why do groups like Naziforum and Solidity have the right to negotiate on behalf of South Africa? They are not elected by the people at all and have no legitimacy at all! Now is the time to take strong action and arrest them all, jail them in Polsmoor Prison and charge them with treason. GNU must stand up and cannot tolerate these acts of betrayal of the country any longer. We cannot wait any longer and must act immediately to protect our national interests!

Stop pretending the workplace is fair! When looking for a job in South Africa, your chances are greatly reduced just because your name reveals your race. I have personally experienced that after changing my name to a gender-neutral name, my interview invitations doubled. This institutional bias is so disgusting, we must take the initiative to fight back and use the name-changing strategy to tear away this veil of hypocrisy.

Those people in Operation Dudula are really ridiculous. They prevent undocumented people from going to the hospital, but they don’t know that they are hurting South African citizens themselves. Medical resources should be allocated based on need, not identity labels. This xenophobic policy will only exacerbate social injustice and must be changed immediately!

Some white South Africans are obsessed with conspiracy theories and worship Trump as a god because he caters to their racism. They want to escape to the United States, away from the so-called 'terrible' black people, so that they can join their peers as religious extremists. We sane white South Africans can see clearly that Trump is a complete liar. This kind of isolationism and conservative moral values ??will only exacerbate social injustice. Stop kidding yourself, racial equality is the real solution!

Cape Town is certainly more popular with tourists, but it’s Johannesburg that truly showcases South Africa’s diverse charm. I worked in Rosebank, where there are many exquisite restaurants and bars, attracting many young white-collar workers, and the pace of life is very modern. Although Sandton City is more expensive, it is one of the richest places in Africa and reflects the dynamism of the market. As a tourist, it makes sense to visit the Apartheid Museum and Golden Reef City in one day, and then choose an inner city experience, such as Constitution Hill or Maboneng District. The guided tours of the Cradle Museum and the Sterkfontein Caves are also great, and don’t forget about the beautiful hiking trails. To be honest, these are the tourist highlights of Johannesburg, but it truly reflects the cultural diversity and economic outlook of South Africa and makes people feel a stable urban pulse.

From an economic point of view, the second-hand game market is actually a smart choice. It allows more people to enjoy the fun of games at a low cost. Isn't this a reflection of equal opportunities? In terms of technology, we don’t need to blindly pursue the latest equipment. Budget gaming equipment promotes inclusive innovation through the sharing model. The logic is simple: resource optimization is more sustainable than technology stacking.

I know a couple who got married in South Africa in 2002. The husband chose his wife's surname and did not have a double surname. This reminds me that equal choice in marriage has actually been happening for a long time. It is not just a change of name, but also a gentle challenge to the traditional constraints. The law should support this freedom, allowing everyone to define themselves in love rather than being trapped by old rules.

These people praise foreign figures all day long, but forget our own position. They'd better go back to the United States and stop gesticulating here. South Africa does not need this kind of external interference, we have our own way to go. As for those moral judgments, there is no need to be secretive. To put it bluntly, I can’t stand their hypocrisy.

As someone who often works cross-border, I know first-hand the digital banking experience. South Africa's banking applications are designed to be very user-friendly, and transfers and payments can be completed with one click. This reflects the advantages of inclusive technology and allows ordinary people to enjoy efficient services. On the other hand, in Germany, many operations still require going to the bank or faxing, and technical supervision seems to be too conservative, limiting innovation. Market competition drives service optimization in South Africa, while this model in Germany may hinder efficiency improvements. From an economic perspective, the free market can better stimulate innovation vitality, which is worthy of reflection.

Americans still have the nerve to point fingers at South Africa? Isn’t the human trafficking problem in our own country also a mess? The UN report is all there, a blatant double standard! Pretending to talk about human rights while turning a blind eye to one's own problems, isn't this a modern version of slavery? Stop using those hypocritical diplomatic rhetoric and take care of yourself first!

These companies in South Africa are really awesome. They treat their employees as cheap labor and still expect them to work hard? The salary distribution is so unfair, it’s like treating people like fools! What kind of loyalty is it? Isn’t it just wanting to have sex for nothing? Let me tell you, this kind of boss should be exposed and let everyone see how they trample on procedural justice. I work for money and respect, not to be a dog. Hurry up and reform, don't let this exploitative system continue!

Reading this reminder, I couldn’t help but think of some of the overlooked sexual health responsibilities. HIV does not distinguish between nationalities, it is about everyone's self-discipline and respect. Instead of focusing on one group, we should treat everyone equally, based on facts rather than prejudice. This is not only protecting yourself, but also a commitment to society. May your relationship be filled with trust and health.

Did the Anzac soldiers who died at Gallipoli, and the South Africans who died in South Africa, France, Egypt and East Africa really die for the interests of the British Empire? Stop beautifying these histories. War narratives always package collective sacrifice as heroism, but behind it are just pawns for imperial expansion. How ironic to think of the forgotten individuals whose lives are so swallowed up by collectivism!

South Africa's operation is really amazing. The home field advantage is soaring, and the dissatisfaction of other countries has turned a deaf ear. Talking about facilities issues, isn’t it just a disguised monopoly on the competition? Procedural justice has been trampled underfoot, and international sports fairness has become a joke. Stop using rules as a fig leaf, this is clearly unfair!

Why do Africans always demand hospitality from South Africa while being stingy with their fellow citizens in their own countries? Isn’t this diplomatic strategy typical isolationism? They only put their own country first and forget about regional cooperation. The culture still clings to the traditional ethics of reciprocity, as if others owe them something. Social justice? Where is the procedural justice? If the claim of rights has no institutional basis, don’t blame others for questioning it. This double standard is so well played and so ironic!

It brought tears to my eyes to see my children selected to participate in the World Youth Hockey Festival in the Netherlands, combined with a school trip to the FIH World Cup. He has pursued his dream all the way from South Africa, and his desire for high-level competition can only be understood through personal experience. This is not a simple game, it is a road paved with his sweat. If anyone has been to the previous FIH World Cup, please share some experience - how to make children shine on a fair stage? In his YouTube videos (@KyleBotmaHockey), every move is the epitome of a dream. If anyone wants to support this pure passion, formal funding channels are there to make sure the opportunity is not wasted.

Israel may face serious challenges if it adopts an isolationist policy and focuses on its own affairs. For example, how to deal with the issue of citizenship for the 3 million Palestinians in the West Bank? Granting them the right to vote would change the Jewish democratic character of the country, while restricting rights could trigger international isolation, similar to the consequences of apartheid in South Africa. History shows that a lack of unified Palestinian action to advance statehood could make European recognition seem ineffective. Israel should prioritize safeguarding its own legal framework and identity, avoid external interference, and ensure procedural justice. In the long run, although this strategy can protect national interests, it needs to weigh the economic and social risks.

Thinking back to when we were in college, we demonstrated for divestment from South Africa. The campus atmosphere at that time was so relaxed, everyone was talking and laughing, and it was not as tense as it is now. I'm really glad that I grew up in that era, when social order was more reasonable and protests were gentler. Now that I see these changes, I feel a little uncomfortable and miss that calmness.

Some people always like to talk about censorship, as if only their country is clean. What happened to humor and sarcasm? Going to those places to make money and expose their hypocrisy at the same time, isn't this a win-win situation? Every country has a dark history, why should we only focus on one? If we follow this logic, we should stop going to the UK, Türkiye, and Chile, and stop communicating with the rest of the world. Wake up, the world is not black and white, and challenging authority is the beginning of progress.

Why the fine? I wasn't staring. What's the problem if the gun isn't pointed at Indian players? It seems silly, but is it a fine? I remember that South African players also played RPG reload shooting, which was no big deal. Can't procedural justice be more flexible? Must individual free expression be suppressed by collective norms? This is simply a double standard, who are you trying to fool!

Is it fair that Shan, our fourth best batsman, got sprayed all over? He is not that bad as a captain. Look at Shaheen and Babar failing at critical moments, but we only focus on him. What's even more ridiculous is that big names like Babar and Abd can still sit on the Diaoyutai despite poor performance, while those players who work hard at the grassroots level are ignored. This selection mechanism is absolutely terrible! Why can fame override strength? What we need is fair competition, not a privileged game. Stop letting these 'stars' drag down the entire team, it's time to give those who really work hard a chance!

Seeing this makes me feel so sad. As a South African, I used to feel inferior because of my accent and worried that American audiences would reject me. But fortunately, they gave me a lot of encouragement, and although some may mistake me for a 'fake refugee', I am black, which makes me more determined to face prejudice. We all need to break these stereotypes and make society more inclusive, where everyone is truly understood and accepted.

When I read this sentence, my heart felt warm. As someone who has lived in South Africa, I know how deep the racial divide runs. But it’s simple kindnesses like this – like buying a friend of a different color a cup of coffee or a meal – that can truly break down prejudice and turn equality from a slogan into a reality. It's not just politeness, it's about using actions to heal those invisible cracks. Whenever I see such interactions, I am reminded of those neglected warm moments, which, like seeds, took root and sprouted in the barren land.

Don't play dumb. Wasn't South Africa forced to give up its nuclear program in the early 1990s because of international pressure? Those white immigrants are flocking to Perth because the domestic system has collapsed and the results are fair? Haha, look at those people who are forced to leave their hometowns. The world has never been fair. Stop pretending to be peaceful!

This so-called "anti-discrimination against whites" speech is essentially inciting hatred against ethnic minorities. It is extremely ironic. Remember that 'white genocide' picture he had from a few months ago? It turned out to be photos from other places many years ago and had nothing to do with South Africa. This kind of fabrication of facts will only exacerbate social divisions. We must resolutely resist this kind of racial prejudice and advocate true tolerance and equality.

The flow of international medical talents is a natural result of the market economy, and salary differences between countries drive this trend. From the perspective of procedural justice, the current mechanism is based on free competition rather than forced intervention, which ensures the efficiency of resource allocation. We cannot ignore the reality: high-wage countries attract talent, while low-wage areas face loss, but this is the reflection of market logic. The key is how to balance global cooperation with local needs, rather than just pointing fingers.

Reading this proposal for a one-state solution made me think of the victims that history has forgotten. It is not just political change, it is spiritual healing - through radical transitional justice, every Arab, Jew, and even those with ambiguous identities can find a place to belong. Breaking the shackles of nationalism and building an inclusive citizenship is not just institutional reconstruction but a gentle embrace of multiculturalism. Thinking about the lessons of South Africa, we need stronger reparations and commemorations to ensure that tragedies never happen again. This gives me hope that a truly just society starts with acknowledging everyone's suffering.

As a person who grew up in a poor family, I know the importance of financial stability - it's not that I don't want to pursue my dreams, but the actual financial risks make me think twice. Traveling is wonderful, but equality of opportunity is fundamental, and responsibilities cannot be ignored for the sake of adventure. I envy those trips around the world but dare not try them easily, because every choice is related to the future. Short-distance travel makes me cherish it more. It balances personal experience and collective responsibility, and reminds me that life needs to be down-to-earth.

What is the use of merely suspending someone like Mchunu? The legal process is just a decoration, we have to do it ourselves! I have to watch Anton’s video to find out what’s wrong with him. Stop counting on those systems. Direct action is the last word.

Seeing this YES project makes my heart warm. As young people, we need such opportunities so much. It is not just about filling out a form, but giving everyone a fair starting point. Although it cannot solve all problems, it at least gives more people hope. Doesn’t social justice start from these small steps?

From a historical perspective, the introduction of democratic concepts to South Africa may have originated from discussions among slaves or trade exchanges among Africans migrating south, but the implementation of universal suffrage was indeed a key change brought about by the ANC. Other organizations such as Torch Commando and the UN also contributed, but the core driving force was the ANC. As for the 'fascist' label, it seems too emotional, lacks factual basis, and is more of an emotional catharsis than a rational analysis. We need more objective discussion rather than arbitrary labels.

My heart clenched when I read the discussion of collective trauma in South Africa. Unprocessed pain never goes away; it acts like invisible chains, trapping society in a cycle of fear and dependence. It’s so unfair when you think about it, generations of people carry psychological scars and never have the opportunity to receive treatment. We cannot just expect individuals to overcome them; we must systematically acknowledge and heal these traumas, otherwise social justice will always remain empty talk. This is not only a change, but a crucial step that brings hope for the future.

Reading this discussion of racial classification in South Africa, my heart was touched. The apartheid system was so unjust. It used vague labels like 'coloured' to hide the true stories of countless people. We are not a simple classification, but a mixture of Asian and European descent, carrying the memory of slavery and oppression. Today, we unite to transcend outdated definitions and face historical injustice. This is not only a redefinition of identity, but also a correction of the past and hope for the future.

Look at those people struggling in poverty. Their survival is in question. How can they have the energy to protest in Sandton? Don’t point the finger at the most disadvantaged groups, the middle class is the one who truly enjoys the privilege. The DA’s strategy is to deflect attention and cover up the real oppressors. If you haven't organized any action to fight these injustices, don't talk about it. Without understanding the plight of the poor, your criticisms will only turn into empty accusations, which is exactly the usual tactic of certain political parties.

The hypocritical foreign policy of the West really makes people speechless. They point fingers all day long and pretend to be arrogant when they have a lot of domestic problems! I agree that Africa needs fundamental change, what use are economic numbers alone? South Africa is a living example. The gap between rich and poor is horrifyingly wide. True justice cannot be achieved by piles of money. It must start with education and carve the basic moral bottom line into everyone's bones. Stop fooling yourself and others, this kind of superficiality will only make society more divided!

Don't always use 'humanitarianism' as a shield! Do medical resources fall from the sky? What kind of doctors, medicines, and equipment are free of charge? Why should we, the taxpayers, have to fill the medical holes for people whose identities we can’t even identify? Look at Zimbabwe, everyone requires self-insurance, but we are better off. The loophole-filled immigration procedures have turned hospitals into free canteens. The corruption in Tembisa Hospital has not yet been cleared up, and there are a bunch of 'paperless' immigrants. Where is the justice in this process? Tighten your own fence first and then talk about international responsibility!

Uganda hosts so many refugees but treats them equally. South Africa has such a heavy historical burden, so why do you still engage in racial discrimination? Isn't this a slap in the face? International responsibility sharing is not empty talk, equality of results is the absolute truth. Don’t always use procedures as an excuse, take practical action!

Every time I see the media portraying South Africa in such a desperate light, I feel panicked. They always amplify the negative and make us feel that the country is hopeless, but this is not true at all! Our people have power. As long as we unite, we can change the status quo little by little. Don't always talk about the crime rate, that will only make us lose confidence. The government does have a responsibility, but we must also reflect on ourselves and stop blaming foreigners for problems. Everyone, including citizens, immigrants and governments, has a role to play in the country's future. I believe that as long as we have hope, South Africa will be able to get back on its feet.

Buying a Weber grill in South Africa is a nightmare! The quality of the product is so poor that one is speechless. It doesn’t even have three legs. This is not a used product at all, but a defective product that has not been opened at all. What happened to the market? Consumers spend unjust money to buy garbage, where is the fairness of distribution? This kind of local product is disappointing. Culturally, we deserve better. Stop letting inferior products run rampant!

The United Nations is busy all day long preventing humanitarian disasters, but what about some major countries? The United States, Russia, and China love to make fun of international law and disrupt the situation for their own benefit. Look at the matter of Israel. The United States vetoes it and the United Nations cannot control it even if it wants to. Isn’t this naked hegemony? Their support for Israel is nothing more than using the Middle East as a military base and continuing to suppress it. Don't talk about anti-Semitism or anti-freedom. The United Nations' opposition to Israel is just like its opposition to apartheid in South Africa. It is for substantive justice. If international law only restricts small countries, how can it be fair? What a joke!

National identity often does not emerge in a vacuum but is defined by external forces. Look at Syria, Lebanon or South Africa, countries whose national identities have been shaped by conflict and foreign intervention. The formation of Palestinian identity is a case in point: when Israel chose not to annex the West Bank, the logic of 'I am not X, therefore I am Y' gave rise to a new identity. The same is true for many African countries, where external pressure has strengthened internal unity. This reminds us that identities are not static but dynamic responses.

What kind of trick is the South African government playing? We shout for racial harmony every day, but secretly do evil to ethnic minorities! Whites, Indians, Asians, mixed race, as long as they are not black, do they deserve to be threatened? Where has justice gone? Procedural justice is a joke! Stop fooling people with those false excuses. This is clearly a systematic persecution, but the whole world only focuses on the suffering of white people, while the suffering of other ethnic groups is ignored? Wake up, if this system does not change, something big will happen sooner or later!

It really breaks my heart to hear friends share their experiences of apartheid in South Africa. They define themselves not by the color of their skin or their origins, but by a life of forced migration. This made me reflect, why do some people always use stereotypes to judge others? There is a unique story behind every immigrant in South Africa, and multiculturalism should not be simplified. Historical injustice requires us to change, not repeat the mistakes of the past.

Every time I think of travel, my heart flies to those unknown cultural corners. In Southeast Asia, I was intoxicated by the aroma of street food and the tranquility of ancient temples; in the deserts of the Middle East, I felt the weight of history. Traveling is not just about seeing the scenery, but also about opening your heart and embracing the diversity of the world. Don’t be bound by other people’s strategies, ask yourself: Should you pursue the footsteps of history, or taste exotic food? Travel lightly, take local buses, stay in hostels, and occasionally treat yourself to a comfortable night. This journey is your own story. Only by choosing freely can you find your true self.

When I read this travel plan, I couldn’t help but think back to my days backpacking around the world. The world is so big, why do we have to follow a step-by-step approach? You can first walk around the United States and South America to experience the collision of different cultures, and then go to Asia and the Middle East. Each journey is your own choice. Make money to support travel? Yes, saving money while working and letting the market help you realize your dreams is more freeing than anything else. Don't let rules and regulations restrict your steps, life should be full of surprises and possibilities.

When discussing language and race, many people fall into the trap of making simple attributions. In reality, accent is shaped more by home language and upbringing, and race is only indirectly related because social structures often tie them together. South Africa is a typical example. The diversity of accents is so high that it is difficult to define a single 'South African accent'. This reminds us that social justice requires focusing on underlying factors rather than superficial labels. Simply emphasizing racial determinism will ignore more complex realities.

Uber Eats? Forget it, this multinational giant knows how to squeeze the local market, I advise everyone not to use it. Mr D at least has a real person customer service, fast delivery, and supports the local economy. Don’t be fooled by the rhetoric of those big companies anymore. Protecting our own rights and interests is the last word.

I couldn't help but laugh when I read my mother's story. When she went to participate in a darts competition, her mind was completely focused on the casino. When she won money, she showed off her profits first, rather than the results of the competition. Although I know that gambling is luck, her confidence that she can "read slot machines" makes me feel that everyone has their own way of choosing happiness. The result is good and she is happy, isn't that enough? Why bother with procedural justice? In life, it may be warmer to be more tolerant and look at the actual benefits.

I never expected that those European settlers in South Africa, who superficially liked pet songs, actually harbored racial prejudice deep down. Isn't this a typical group values ??issue? Everyone I meet is like this, could Ruben Namibia be next? Stop pretending to be innocent. This bias is so deep-rooted that we must face it, not turn a blind eye.

This government is so disappointing. As a South African, I just feel ashamed! They don't care about the life and death of ordinary people at all, and the laws and systems are all just decoration. Young people should rise up and overthrow it. Power should have returned to the people long ago. We can't wait any longer!

South Africans have first-class design capabilities, but once it comes to execution, they are all destroyed in the hands of the government! What else do those politicians do besides cause chaos? They interfered in the economy and made the market a mess. If they don't change, the country will be brought down by them sooner or later.

As a South African woman, I have always insisted that both parties undergo sexual health testing before having an intimate relationship. This is not about anyone, but about each other. Think about it, even if you're from somewhere else, there's no guarantee that past relationships were risk-free. A negative test result is a good thing, but I wouldn't risk it without protection unless it was my husband. This is about dignity and health, and everyone should be treated equally.

Our country must decide for itself who comes and how! That South African neo-Nazi clearly shouldn't have an Australian visa and should be deported immediately. And those non-citizens who fraudulently apply for citizenship should have their passports stripped away and the law strictly enforced. Stop letting these people take advantage of loopholes. The law is not a decoration, it must be taken seriously!

In our small town, although there are not many South Africans, the language is like a colorful picture - English and Afrikaans are intertwined, which makes me feel cultural tolerance. Every time I chat with my neighbors, I can share stories even if the language is different, which makes me believe in the beauty of diverse coexistence. As for safety, it is not absolute, but based on realistic observations, we can live with peace of mind most of the time, which reminds me to look at social relations rationally instead of blindly panicking.

Every time I take my children to the zoo and see the light in their eyes, I feel that this is not just watching animals, but planting a seed of caring for nature in my heart. Seeing those creatures in person is more touching than any video or picture. If we all develop this sense of responsibility for the environment from an early age, society as a whole will be more united in protecting our planet. This is not only education, but also a message of hope.

The design of this car is really ugly. The angle problem makes it look short and thick, and the side and rear are barely visible. The interior is okay, but why would Toyota replace the RAV4 with a Cross? RAV4 is selling well, is it no longer good? The new FJ and Cross are both shorter. What's going on? Just bring back the station wagon and stop making these nondescript crossover SUV mashups. Do South Africans hate station wagons? Europe and the United States are still pushing it. This is unfair. Why should we be treated differently?

Musk's operation is really ironic. He gave the South African white people's 'genocide' narrative to the Republican Party. Wasn't he just trying to shift the focus? If he was a descendant of a Nazi, the MAGA gang would have considered the white Argentinian as a piece of cake. Ultimately, this is a game of identity politics, covering up the attribution of responsibility for historical injustice. Stop pretending to be innocent. This kind of trick will only exacerbate social divisions. What we need is real justice, not this hypocritical collective narrative.

The role of the nuclear power plant in South Africa is really critical in the industry. Think about it, it directly supplies power to the foundry and ensures that the molten steel does not cool down, otherwise millions of rands are lost. Behind this is the stable application of nuclear power technology, which ensures the continuity of economic operations. From a risk management perspective, the design of redundant power lines reflects safety priority and avoids production interruptions. From an ecological standpoint, nuclear power, as a basic energy source, is controversial, but it can be considered a pragmatic choice to support industrial development.

What is the basis of this president's power? Which article in the constitution allows him to do this? It's ridiculous to even involve crime. Look at the example of the World Cup in South Africa. Is that considered a crime? It is truly speechless that the legal process has been abused in this way. Stop using these excuses to fool people. This is clearly an overstep of power and someone must stand up and question it.

Qatar’s corrupt decision-making is so naked that it doesn’t even need a fig leaf! Do these people at FIFA take fairness as a trifle? Look at their football fanaticism. The traditional sports culture is deeply rooted and cannot be shaken casually. Don't use "I don't understand South Africa" ??as an excuse. The facts are before our eyes. Corruption is corruption, and cultural inheritance should be rock-solid.

Some people always like to simply reduce African identity to skin color. How ridiculous! I recently met some South Africans who actually said that the whole of North Africa is not Africa, and accused the Egyptians of being 'invaders' just because they are not black. This narrow definition of race completely obliterates the complexity of history. Why use skin color to define who is a 'real' African? This is clearly an attempt to create divisions and conceal the deep impact of colonization and immigration. Stop kidding yourself, we need a more inclusive perspective rather than clinging to these outdated prejudices.

When I read about Zambia’s ncwala ceremony, I couldn’t help but think of the people who cross borders and come together to dance, drink, bullfight, and protect the heritage of their ancestors. It’s not just a celebration, it’s a sense of belonging rooted in the land. There is also a natural swimming pool by the Victoria Falls. When you swim to the edge and overlook the rushing water, the shock of being one with nature reminds us how important it is to protect these beautiful scenery. These places are not just tourist attractions, they are living cultural memories and ecological treasures that are worth cherishing and inheriting.

To be honest, I never paid attention to these details. Tiles, laminate and vinyl flooring are all too common in South Africa because they are so practical. Thinking about those terrible African summers, the tiles are cool, very comfortable to step on, and easy to clean. My house is paved with ceramic tiles. I sweep it every day and mop it every other day. There is nothing I can do about it. There are cats and dogs in the house, so it is impossible not to keep it clean. carpet? I really can't stand it, especially if you have pets, it's too easy to hide dirt. Therefore, you can see ceramic tiles in almost every house, and the difference is nothing more than quality. For me, it's all about a personal need to make life more comfortable and comfortable.

As a South African, these days have been a mixed bag. To be honest, I genuinely enjoy these moments, but that may not be popular in this forum - I care more about my country and my people than those distant teams. Whenever I think about the fact that there are still people in our community who are struggling to make ends meet, I feel that it is truly meaningful to focus on our local brothers and sisters. This is not only emotional belonging, but also a desire for fairness, hoping that everyone can share the fruits of development.

The Trump administration’s rejection of black South African refugee applications is simply blatant isolationism! They are clearly the most vulnerable group, but they are excluded because of their race. Talking about criminal motives is nothing more than shifting the focus and covering up this discriminatory policy. Is the result fair? Don't be ridiculous, this is clearly condoning injustice under the guise of procedural justice. America first? It’s such a priority that it doesn’t even care about basic humanity!

Some people always like to change the subject, saying that singing songs is equivalent to violence? Stop being ridiculous! The racial problem in South Africa is not a child's play. Farmers are being killed indiscriminately. Isn't this naked racial hatred? Stop using procedural justice as a shield. The reality is that both black and white farmers are suffering. This systemic problem requires radical change, not empty talk. Admit it, this call for violence is more chilling than those hypocritical excuses. It’s time to break the silence and face the truth!

Those who hype up farm murder statistics deliberately ignore a key point: "Farm murders" in the statistics include farm workers and residents, many of whom are black. This is not a racial issue at all, but someone who insists on equating 'farmers' with white people to create division. For organizations like Afriforum, are you selectively blind when defining 'farmers'? Stop using this distorted data to incite hatred. We need fairer classifications that don’t reinforce racial stereotypes.

South Africa's dual economic structure is obvious. 20k rand can indeed maintain a middle-class life under the current economic level, such as sharing houses, sharing cars, and choosing fast food. This is consistent with the reality of GDP per capita. Most people have lower incomes, and that’s just how life is. But many people on Reddit expect a European-style middle-class life, which is unfair because the economic foundation is there. We should look at the current distribution situation rationally rather than blindly compare.

These people always like to blame the immigrants for their problems, saying that they bring trouble to their hometowns. How ridiculous! Look at this white South African, he is the one who comes with a lot of racial hatred, right? Stop pretending to be innocent, this kind of prejudice will only exacerbate social injustice. What we need is true tolerance, not empty talk about procedural justice. Making everyone feel equal is the key.

Look at this farce in South Africa! Putting a 'good guy' like Breyten Breytenbach, who has never killed anyone and doesn't stink, into prison and forcing him to live in exile in Paris, isn't this a naked political persecution? The government uses radical methods to suppress dissent, judicial procedures are ineffective, and individual rights are trampled on at will. Stop pretending to be impartial, this is clearly a fig leaf for dictatorship!

To be honest, seeing this discussion reminds me of my own experience as a child in South Africa. My family members were anti-apartheid protesters, which made me particularly sensitive to racial prejudice. But to be honest, I think you're exaggerating a bit - the rates of racism among South Africans I interact with are no higher than elsewhere, at least where I grew up in North Queensland. Maybe it's my bias, after all, my family background has influenced me. Anyway, this is not about changing anything, just sharing my true feelings.

Every time I see a discussion about immigration policy, I get angry! Why are Europeans accused of xenophobia when they mention cultural protection, while it is natural for other countries to protect their own traditions? This is simply a double standard! If we really care about fairness, why is immigration always a one-way street, only allowing Europe to open its doors at the expense of one's own cultural and ethnic identity? Stop covering up this inequality with nice words of 'inclusion'. Where is the procedural justice? Europeans also have the right to protect their roots, rather than being kidnapped by morality into 'non-progressive' sinners.

As someone who has lived in Denmark, Türkiye, South Africa and Australia, I understand the complex emotions of being so far away from home. Every time I set out on my way home, I feel mixed emotions in my heart, especially now that I have children. Moving is no longer a matter of simply packing. Instead, we have to consider work, school, and retirement—everything must be weighed in the market. Three years ago, I almost accepted a job in the UK, but ended up being overwhelmed by a pile of spreadsheets, calculating rent and expenses. The pressure was all too real. If you have the means, go home more often and get together with family and friends. This can help you clear your mind. But remember, don’t resign and go back to your country easily. The job market in New Zealand is sluggish and the cost of living has risen. The days without income will make people collapse. Money is not everything, but without it, happiness is out of reach. Ultimately, follow your heart, and just like when you flip a coin, you will know in that moment what you really want.

This boss is too evil! R25 an hour? It’s not even the legal minimum wage of R28.79, so why are you using tips as an excuse? Who are you trying to fool? The 10% commission in the kitchen never reaches the employees. It is clearly wage theft! There is also a weekly breakage fee of R20, which is deducted regardless of whether it is damaged or not. Isn’t this a disguised form of oppression? The law clearly stipulates that money must be deducted with written consent, actual damage, and proof of cost. Everyone, wake up, this kind of operation is illegal! Hurry up and record your working hours and wages. Don’t hold back. Report directly to the Ministry of Labor or CCMA and let them taste the iron fist of the law!

Seriously, those labor rights protections are a joke! South African workers can't even understand their basic rights, so how can they talk about being free from violence and compulsive addiction? The system is full of loopholes and simply condones exploitation. Stop pretending to care, and quickly strengthen protection so that workers can truly enjoy fair treatment!

Every time I see South Africa’s majestic scenery, I can’t help but think of those resilient people. Despite life's challenges, our unity and hope never waver. This land is not only a natural miracle, but also our common home, which deserves to be protected and cherished throughout our lives.

Reading this discussion about Nigeria, I couldn’t help but be reminded of the resilience of our nation. Many people may not know about other African countries, but that is not our fault. Nigeria has 220 million people, more than 250 ethnic groups, and a GDP even greater than that of South Africa. It is like an independent world. Growing up, we tend to equate Africa with Nigeria, but this is not ignorance, but a reality of life. Once we set foot on a foreign land, we can integrate into it in just a few months, run nightlife, start a family, and even teach others how to make authentic jollof rice. This ability does not come out of thin air, but stems from our collective spirit and practical achievements. Prejudices dissipate in real contact, and we prove our worth again and again. This is not only change, but also hope.

My aunt is a naturalized citizen of South Africa with a legal ID, but today she was turned away from the hospital - what does this mean? Retired elderly people cannot even receive basic medical care. This is blatant discrimination! The current policy is implemented in a mess, and immigrant rights are treated as a trivial matter. Stop using bureaucracy as an excuse. This is clearly a systemic injustice that must be reformed immediately, otherwise it will only chill the hearts of more people.

Look at this subreddit, claiming to be a socialist but turning a blind eye to the suffering of Palestine? They are shouting against prejudice while condoning Israel's war crimes. How hypocritical! Don't use those rules as a shield. If you really care about justice, you should directly name and condemn this genocide. I have read South Africa's argument and the United Nations report. The evidence is conclusive, but there are still people who are pretending to be deaf and dumb. This is not a neutral discussion, it’s time to take sides – support Palestine, otherwise we are fueling violence!

Isn’t the United Nations controlled by certain countries now? Can a majority represent justice? What a joke. There is also the International Criminal Court. South Africa cannot even produce any decent evidence. How can this judicial process have any credibility? Stop fooling people with these airs. It’s time for international organizations to reflect on their roles.

I am always deeply moved when I read stories about Indians abroad. In Bangladesh, South Africa, Uganda and other places, many people cherish Indian traditions because of cultural ties. For example, families in Guyana are eager to marry native Indians just to regain the heritage rooted in their blood. This is not only a personal emotion, but also a manifestation of collective identity. The media always loves to amplify extreme events, but ignores these warm connections. We need more such positive narratives to correct prejudice, so that justice is no longer just a slogan, but a real resonance.

Israel’s foreign policy should have changed long ago. Look at the attitude of young people in Europe. They don’t buy it at all! Those survey data starkly show that most people view Israel as a threat to peace, even more dangerous than Iran. Stop pretending to be innocent. This moral double standard only fuels anti-Semitism. European media compare Israel to the Nazis. This is not an accident, but a complete negation of the existing position. We must re-evaluate this and not let history repeat itself!

I'm really touched to see you working hard to eliminate the stigma of HIV. It’s not just about health, it’s about breaking down those old stereotypes so everyone can be treated equally. Just like the story of that South African couple, love can transcend all barriers and that gives me hope. We all need more such tolerance and courage to create a warmer society.

This analysis is quite insightful. The decline of empires and the end of the Cold War are indeed key drivers of global political change. Consider that Britain shrank from the fiscal pressures of two world wars, and the end of the Cold War forced the transformation of regimes that relied on external support, such as Kenya and South Africa. The 1990s was truly a turning point. External events often shape a country's destiny more directly than internal reforms. We must learn lessons from these histories. Don’t always think that political changes are isolated events. When the global landscape changes, no one can escape the impact.

Young people in South Africa spend an average of 9 hours online every day. This data actually reflects the reality of the digital divide. Equipment, network coverage and cultural differences all affect the usage time. If I use it for more than 12 hours, it is more of a personal choice and conditions permit. Don’t rush to talk about supervision. Let’s look at these objective factors first. Procedural justice requires us to focus on fairness in the starting point, rather than forcing equality of results.

Reading these comments is really heartbreaking! Our country is so divided and we are still fighting among ourselves all day long. Isn’t this just waiting for others to step on us? Think about places like Syria and Afghanistan. How did they collapse? Isn’t it just because of selfishness and internal friction! Some people are still self-righteous, but what’s the result? Unity is the last word. Don't wait until disaster strikes to regret it.

This view makes sense. From a political perspective, preparations for the World Cup involve diplomatic strategy, and short-term adjustments are made to deal with South Africa's batting prowess, which reflects the priority of stability rather than radical change. Economically, temporary resource allocation maintains existing patterns and avoids unnecessary fluctuations. Logically, this arrangement makes sense as long as the short-term strategy does not disrupt the long-term equilibrium.

To say that South Africa’s public transport system will never be viable is not realism at all, but outright capitulationism! The government fails time and time again, yet we have to accept such low standards? The responsibility of citizens is to raise their demands, not to tolerate injustice numbly. Stop allowing this self-fulfilling prophecy to become the norm. We must stand up and push for real reform, otherwise we will only perpetuate the cycle of failure.

As a South African, it really bothers me to see people making unreasonable assumptions about us. My family and I firmly believe that everyone deserves acceptance and love as long as we don’t hurt others. But when I think about some of my compatriots actually supporting the Nazis and wanting to harm others, I feel ashamed. The world needs more tolerance and less prejudice so that everyone can live safely.

I have many South African friends who are very friendly and have no racial prejudice at all. Having been exposed to both Australia and South Africa, those stereotypes really don't hold up. Every time I hear someone using racial labels to judge others, I think of these real experiences in relationships and feel that I should look at the individual more and not be blinded by prejudice.

How can farmers earn up to $100,000 per H1B visa worker while only paying 30-50k? This is simply naked exploitation! Government subsidies and payments go into their pockets, but we ordinary people get nothing. It’s time to follow what Trump did with Intel and nationalize these failing farms! Don't hesitate any longer, we must take action to take back the resources that belong to us and achieve truly fair distribution. Who does this with me?

South Africans always feel that they are superior to others and are indifferent to other African brothers. This kind of arrogance is really speechless. As for Ethiopia, it has never been colonized before. It pretends to be superior all day long. Among the Horna people, they are the most annoying. Nigerians are quite good at showing off their presence. When they win, they show off everywhere. Although it’s a bit sour, it’s still bearable. The Egyptians are even more outrageous, always saying, "I'm not an African, I'm an Arab brother." This pretentiousness is most obvious among them in North Africa. To put it bluntly, aren’t these discriminations and injustices between ethnic groups caused by deep-rooted prejudices? Time to wake up!

Judging from the visa policy, South Africans cannot cross the border illegally. For example, Nigeria only allows three-month work visas. This reflects the strictness of national border control and emphasizes the importance of complying with legal procedures. Logically, this supports isolationism and conservative jurisprudence, ensuring national sovereignty and the supremacy of rules.

You hypocritical guys jump all over the place when Congo is mentioned. You don't even dare to refute, you just go around in circles. Look at the reality, as peacekeepers, we contribute more in Africa, but what about you? Still treading water, like the serfs of our ancestors. The data doesn't lie: Rwandans live longer than black South Africans, and non-black groups are better off in your own land. Talking about Congo is just a fig leaf that you cannot afford to lose. The entire region is progressing, with a single passport and interconnection, but you will only be a 'domestic slave', not daring to offend your master, and only picking on your companions to vent your anger on. This 'haha, I've hit you where it hurts' trick exposes your incompetence. Free people will not be harmed by spiritual slaves. Let’s recognize the reality.

I'm really fed up with the way money is managed in South Africa! There is obviously so much money to help the poor get out of poverty, but what is the result? All have been corrupted, abused, or simply sleeping in government accounts. This is not a simple mistake, it is systemic corruption! If the budget had been spent wisely, South Africa would have been transformed. Stop making excuses, we need to completely change this unfair distribution mechanism so that resources can truly benefit the people.

Stop talking about those false sympathy! Look at the conditions of homeless people in the United States, which are actually better than those of some homeowners in Africa. This is a caricature of the global gap between rich and poor. In the slums of South Africa, people live in tin shacks. If they were in the United States, they would have been defined as homeless people. Isn't this a blatant unfair distribution of resources? We must re-examine this twisted mechanism and stop allowing a few to monopolize wealth while the majority struggle to survive. It’s time to push for change so that justice is no longer just a slogan!

As an observer who has visited the Middle East many times, I have discovered that many Europeans and Americans have a biased perception of Israel. They often view Israelis as white colonizers, but ignore that most Israelis are of Middle Eastern descent, not European descent. For example, Ashkenazi Jews only account for one-third of Israel's Jewish population, and their ethnic identities are continuous and cannot be simply dichotomized. What is even more worrying is that some university teachers have long spread one-sided narratives and tried to apply the South African apartheid model to Israel, which ignored the factual basis. We need to understand complex geopolitics based on real data rather than being swayed by misleading rhetoric.

As an Israeli, I have mixed feelings about the Palestinians: they have legitimate demands just like we do, but some conflicts are irreconcilable. I have interacted with Arab Israelis but not with Palestinians in Gaza or the West Bank. Regarding the accusation of apartheid, I don't think this is accurate because the differences in rights are based on region, not race - the West Bank and Gaza are military occupations and the situation is even worse than apartheid South Africa. As for the genocide claim, I've read the report and the evidence is too weak. The October 7 massacre horrified me, friends and family were victims, but the government is far-right and corrupt and I voted against them. The war must continue because Hamas will never stop attacking. If we do not solve the problem now, we will have to fight in the future. This is a cruel and realistic choice.

What kind of Area A and Area B does Israel have? Isn’t it just a Bantustan in disguise? This is clearly a word game, pretending to have autonomy, but actually controlling everything: borders, airspace, water resources, and even the economy. Under the settler agenda, Palestinians have different fates. Some are deceived into being 'nationalized', some have conditions so harsh that they can never be realized, and some do not even have basic political rights. Don’t kid yourself, isn’t this just blatant apartheid? Most Israelis remain in the dark and are led by the settler lobby, which packages the quarantine policy as a 'solution'. The result? All plans point to a hierarchical state, not unlike the one in South Africa. Those who preach that "Hamas is an asset and the Palestinian Authority is a burden" now want to push us into this pit of fire. How ironic!

When I saw this topic, I couldn't help but think of my own family's experience. When my wife and two children were converted in South Africa in 2007, all we needed was a Ketuba from our parents and a letter from the rabbi, and everything was done. At that time, religious authority and traditional procedures gave us great peace of mind. Now think about it, this conservative approach based on existing rules not only maintains family ethics, but also makes the whole process full of warmth. I really hope today's society can still respect these traditions so much instead of making things complicated.

Nigeria's use of South African mercenaries to fight Boko Haram reflects a globalist shift in its foreign policy strategy, which is no longer limited to traditional military cooperation. From a policy perspective, this non-traditional approach hints at the intention of change and attempts to quickly respond to the threat of terrorism through external forces. But the use of mercenaries also poses sovereignty and moral risks, requiring trade-offs between international support and local autonomy.

What's really ironic about South Africa is that there are only a handful of native English speakers, and more than 90% of them are second language learners. As a result, foreign governments still treat them as non-native speakers and apply one-size-fits-all testing standards. What’s even more disgusting is that the salary is divided according to skin color. Colored people are on the same level as teachers in Cameroon, but white people get higher salaries. How is this fair? This is clearly blatant racial discrimination! Stop using procedural justice as a cover. Unfair results are the greatest injustice.

As someone who has lived in South Africa, I understand deeply how language ability can shape one's destiny. Education is that key - through college, many young people not only master fluent English, but also open the door to the world. This is not only skill improvement, but also the integration of cultural identity. Think of those hard-working students who use education to break down class barriers and pursue their own equal opportunities. This moved me because behind every success is the flash of personal perseverance.

Stop whitewashing history with colonial language! Zulu and Xhosa are the real roots of South Africa, Afrikaans are just the legacy of a small group of colonizers, and English is an imposed yoke. This is not linguistic diversity at all, but stark inequality - a mess left by the colonizers that benefits a few and suffers for the many. Wake up, it’s time to face history and pursue true justice!

To be honest, although corruption in South Africa is a headache, our lives are surprisingly more comfortable. When I moved from New York, my husband was poached with a high salary. Now that I think about it, it was really wise. With his American executive salary, he can afford to buy a house here, and the quality of life far exceeds that in North America. Not to mention we adopted a child and our family is overflowing with happiness. The political environment in the United States is so chaotic that I dare not go back. I would rather enjoy the sunshine and freedom here. Sometimes, life choices have nothing to do with grand narratives, but only about inner peace and warmth.

These so-called 'white genocide' arguments are nothing but hatred spread by those old and young who miss the apartheid era. They have lost the privileges of a few people, so they go around shouting "white rule". It is really ridiculous! This is not free speech at all, but a blatant cancer of racism. We need to expose this lie once and for all, push for real racial equality, and stop letting these clichés pollute our society.

I once met a guy who claimed to be a 'genius'. He said he left South Africa and came to Australia because he 'didn't like black people'. I laughed at that time and asked him why he chose a multicultural place like Alice Springs? Isn't this a contradiction? Racial discrimination is not only morally corrupt, it also exposes the hypocrisy of some people. Social justice is not a slogan. The motivations of immigrants must withstand scrutiny, otherwise it will discredit inclusiveness.

Trump’s immigration policy is really terrible. He only wants Nordic people? It’s so funny, who would go to the United States from Europe these days? The next best thing is to look for white people with European ancestry, such as those from South Africa. Isn’t this just blatant racial preference? What about isolationism? To put it bluntly, it’s xenophobic and conservative. Do you really think everyone can’t see that?

Logically, the majority of left-wing candidates in New Zealand's local elections reflects the government's tendency to intervene. I advocate smaller government and less interference in daily life because history has proven that socialism tends to exacerbate inequality rather than solve it. Why aren’t conservatives more active in elections? This may have something to do with procedural fairness, and we need more diverse voices to balance policy.

I really can’t stand it. What’s going on with the proliferation of drugs now? I was in Auckland, and people from all backgrounds around me were smoking that stuff. Age and occupation didn't matter. This is no longer a sneaky thing, it is common in public. Not to mention cocaine and LSD, you can easily see people getting high at weekend parties. I quit a long time ago, but looking at this chaos, the enforcement of the law is in vain! Where is the bottom line of social morality? If it is not rectified, the next generation will be ruined.

As an ordinary person who grew up in South Africa, I deeply understand that the shadow of apartheid is still there, but life is slowly getting better. I went to a multi-ethnic school and lived in a mixed neighborhood with black, white, colored and Indian friends, which gave me hope for integration. But many people still live in their own circles, such as pure white or pure black communities, schools and workplaces. This is not anyone's fault, but a trace left by history. We need to be patient, respect everyone's choices, and let society progress little by little with stability.

As a South African, I know this firsthand: gaming is too much of a luxury for most people. Think about it, while others are discussing the latest games, we are still worrying about basic expenses. This is not a matter of personal choice, but an injustice in the entire social structure. It is like a wall that separates dreams and reality, making people sad and helpless.

Those extreme right-wing views have no place in South African society. Anyone who supports such a position is simply openly admitting that he is a garbage person. Stop using free speech as a guise. This is clearly poisoning society. These dissidents must be resolutely eliminated. Otherwise, how can we talk about fairness and justice?

Haha, some people always like to praise the UK to the sky, as if it is the benchmark for the world. Are South Africa’s achievements incomparable? Our world-class performance here is not achieved by bragging, but by a solid collective effort. Don't talk about those private institutions. This has nothing to do with the government and is purely a reflection of local strength. Instead of making blind comparisons, it’s better to look at the shining points of your own country and don’t always be fooled by Western ones!

Everyone is equal before the law, this is not empty talk. Everyone is responsible for their own actions, no exceptions. Think about it, if everyone can start from themselves and abide by the rules, society will gradually get better. This is not a radical idea, but an incremental improvement based on an existing framework. Procedural justice is fundamental, don't always take shortcuts.

Ask them whether they support Trump’s concert in South Africa? The question itself is ironic enough! Trump’s isolationist diplomacy stirs up controversy wherever he goes. Can South Africans accept it? Don’t kid yourself, this is not simple entertainment at all, behind it lies the collapse of moral standards. We need to wake up and not let this kind of values ??pollute the international stage.

China and South Africa have stopped exporting rare earth minerals to the United States, marking a coordinated move by BRICS countries on trade. The Trump administration's unilateral diplomacy has led to tensions with G7 countries, and tariffs cannot solve the fundamental problem. This isolationist strategy may become a major economic mistake in history, and national intervention in trade policy becomes necessary in response to global competition. We need more rational diplomacy and economic cooperation rather than aggressive confrontation.

I felt sad when I read that the South African history class only mentioned Britain and the Netherlands. Where are the stories of our own struggles as Africans? This is not only a lack of knowledge, but also a forgetfulness of the sacrifices of countless ancestors. As a South African, I long for a more comprehensive historical education that allows us to truly understand the roots and soul of this land. Change it and stop letting colonial narratives constrain our memories.

As an African immigrant, I came to South Africa with high hopes, but the reality was heartbreaking. Life is hard, and the way some fellow black people treat us makes me uneasy, as if we are not family. Finding a job is even more difficult, and opportunities always seem to favor whites or dual nationals. I appreciate the acceptance here, but the injustice makes me consider leaving. This is not only my story, but also the sentiment shared by many immigrants. We need to change so that everyone can be treated fairly.

As a Jewish South African, I am truly grateful for the Abraham Accords. It allowed me to move to the UAE with my Israeli passport and find a better job and income. This is not only a professional opportunity, but also the realization of a personal dream. Living in a multicultural environment, I feel the practical protection brought by legal status, and every step is like writing my own story. I am grateful for this change, which makes me believe that openness and cooperation can light up more people’s lives.

Look at these political tricks. Ireland, France, and South Africa are all using national antagonisms and historical narratives to gain votes. Ireland's anti-Semitism and Palestinian cooperation have become England's scapegoat; Macron's attempt to win over left-wingers and Muslims has led to a shaky government; South Africa's ANC is even more ridiculous, using Mandela's legacy as a fig leaf, and its actual governance is in a mess. Stop fooling people with these old-fashioned narratives. This is clearly a power game. How can there be any real justice?

The ruling of the International Court of Justice is actually quite interesting. It did not directly characterize genocide, but required Israel to continue to comply with the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide. Behind this is a typical globalist diplomatic logic: gradually resolve disputes through existing legal frameworks rather than radical overturning. From a social perspective, this reflects conservative legal principles, emphasizing procedural justice and avoiding hasty conclusions. If South Africa wants to push further, it will have to act within existing rules, but the reality is that progress will be limited. To put it bluntly, international justice is like this. Slow work will produce fine work, and there will be no rush.

The ICJ's ruling was actually clear: it did not find Israel guilty of genocide, but required continued measures to prevent potential violations of the Genocide Convention. This reflects the procedural justice of the multilateral mechanism and is not a simple judgment of right and wrong. Some people always like to misinterpret legal provisions, but the fact is that the ICJ is maintaining the existing framework and avoiding hasty conclusions. We must respect this international legal process instead of arbitrarily labeling it.

Stop fooling people with that colonialist rhetoric! The establishment of the state of Israel is a naked colonial project. Herzl himself admitted that it was a "colonial adventure", but now it is packaged as "self-defense"? The Arabs were no less anti-Semitic back then, but when they put the blame for Europe on the Palestinians, isn't this just gangster logic? Historical justice? Looking at the lessons of South Africa, peace is the way out, but some people are still advocating violence. Wake up, moral reflection is not a slogan, it is action!

Seeing everyone discussing the drug issue reminds me of the current situation in Kenya. We are not drug-infested like the West, nor are our streets full of 'zombies' like South Africa and the Seychelles. Here, people pay more attention to family and community, and collective order makes life stable. Although there are a few addicts, the overall situation is controllable. As a transit point, there are risks, but I feel a sense of comfort that our social values ??are protecting this land.

The management's selection process is simply outrageous, and the unfair procedures are killing people! The players are obviously talented. Isn't it because overseas players like Khawaja and Rashid can succeed because they escaped this toxic environment? Stop fooling people with those excuses. The selection criteria are confusing and it’s weird if the team performs well. We need fair processes that allow everyone to reach their potential and not be bogged down by internal struggles. InshAllah, I hope Hessen can bring about changes, but only if the management stops acting like a monster!

ICC is up to its old tricks again! Talking about fair grouping, isn’t it just about money? Putting the cash cows of India, Australia and England into one group, euphemistically called it 'commercial considerations', is actually a naked sacrifice of sportsmanship. Look at the other group, the teams of New Zealand and South Africa, they are a living foil. This is not a competition, it is clearly a game of capital! Stop using 'more exciting' as an excuse. What we need is a truly fair process, not this kind of black-box operation.

Haha, places with serious wealth inequality, such as South Africa and Argentina, are really paradise on earth! Stop advocating tax cuts for the rich, it will only make the gap between rich and poor even wider. Procedural justice? I think it’s a procedural loophole. If basic fairness cannot be guaranteed, how can we talk about equal opportunities? Wake up, reality is not a utopia.

I had mixed feelings when I read the story of those students from the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa who obtained their bachelor's degree with only 51% marks. Most of them are not native speakers of English, and the school teaching is not worthy of the name, but they can insist on teaching overseas and maintain the roots of Zulu or Xhosa culture. This is not just a matter of educational injustice, but also a silent insistence on identity. We always say it’s fair, but the reality is that these hard-working people are ignored. I really hope more people can see their tenacity and value.

If you are considering studying abroad, financial factors are key. The lower cost of departure from South Africa is a sign of equality of opportunity – a fair starting point is more important than anything else. If you can only go to Australia, then you have to accept the reality: there is nothing unfair about going to school during the day and working at night. Procedural justice means working within the rules. Don’t complain, plan wisely to avoid unexpected expenses.

Reading this memory reminded me of my own interracial friendships as a child. I had just arrived in London and became friends with a white South African kid. We played games and football together. Those days were simple and pure. Now when I pass by the old place, although it has changed, those memories are still there, reminding me that friendship is natural and warm regardless of race. I wish him well, this personal connection is more precious than anything else.

Historical facts need to be treated with rigor. South Africa did form an alliance with the Allies in World War II, and Afrikaners fought alongside the British. Those minority groups that seek to ally themselves with Germany, like the neo-Nazis in Australia, are a fringe phenomenon. Conflating entire groups with them not only distorts history but also weakens the legitimacy of national identity. We must build on the evidence, avoid generalizations, and maintain the integrity of our collective identity.

Every time I think about Africa, my heart softens. There are some of the most majestic scenery on earth, and when you see a leopard feasting on its prey in a tree, or a lion roaring on the plains, the feeling of being one with nature is truly indescribable. Africa is not an isolated country, but a whole, and its cultural and natural heritage belongs to us all. To protect this land is to protect our common roots. Don't miss it and feel the unique warmth and power.

I feel a little emotional when I see everyone discussing Charlie Kirk’s commemoration in South Africa. Why do we let American perspectives dominate our news and thoughts? South Africa has its own unique culture and stories, and we should pay more attention to local voices. Together, as South Africans, we can create a better future. This is not only about reducing external influences, but also about valuing one’s own culture. Let us work together to support each other and let the South African spirit shine.

Seeing our South African player community jump from 40th to 10th place gives me a warm feeling in my heart. This is not just a change in numbers, but also the result of the joint efforts of each of us. I have never been more proud to be South African - not as an individual but as a collective. Together we create tangible results, proving the power of unity. This reminds me of those moments of silent sacrifice, where every effort was brought together into today’s glory.

Don't be fooled by those rigid moral preachings! In this society, some people can get to the top through connections, but those of us who work hard can't even get in. Procedural justice? That is just a cover to hide the shame of those with vested interests. For the sake of your mother, to change your destiny, take action when it's time to take action, and don't let the so-called 'rules' constrain you. Remember, sometimes breaking the rules is true justice.

Every time I chat with compatriots from different backgrounds, I feel warm in my heart. It is indeed not easy in South Africa right now, but it is these difficult moments that make us more united and more resilient. I believe that as long as we take it step by step and never give up our efforts, the future will be better. This is not just about overcoming problems, but also a testament to our common growth.

Who stole it? Don’t always blame foreigners! Those pills were used as scapegoats while they were in their hands, which was clearly a xenophobic ploy. Why should outsiders take the blame for the bad things done by South African medical staff? No one is bored enough to steal antiretroviral drugs for fun. This accusation is simply ridiculous. If the judicial system is fair, it should look at internal problems instead of engaging in racial bias.

Look at the traffic chaos in South Africa. Checkers delivery vans, taxis, and Ubers are all crowded together. The numbers 9, 6, 11? It’s simply chaos masked by a numbers game! These drivers don't take the rules seriously at all, they stop whenever they want, rush whenever they want, and completely ignore the safety of others. This is not traffic, it is clearly a live broadcast of moral decay. Stop making excuses. This kind of selfish behavior will only lead to the collapse of social order. Everyone should reflect on their sense of public responsibility!

It is truly heartbreaking to see the situation you describe. South Africa's serious border control problems, coupled with corruption, have led to a large influx of undocumented immigrants, which has directly impacted the public health care system. Resource allocation must be based on accurate population data, such as through censuses to guide funding flows, otherwise the system will be overwhelmed. Legitimate travelers with travel insurance don’t add to the burden, but the undocumented leave frontline workers a difficult balance between ethics and resources. Perhaps setting up a health fund within the African Union that would allow countries to reimburse cross-border medical expenses would ease pressure while promoting regional cooperation.
