They have done a good job, but shouldn’t France’s testing of nuclear bombs in Africa alarm African countries? We can no longer rely on foreign powers! South Africa gave up its nuclear weapons and is now subject to others everywhere. Africa must have its own nuclear weapons. This is a fundamental change and cannot wait any longer! Only when you have autonomy in your own hands can you face the world straight.

The polarization of American society is simply speechless. The rich and the poor live in different worlds, and car dependence is just the tip of the iceberg. Look at those collectivist countries, everyone is more united, unlike here who only care about themselves. It’s time to completely change this selfish pattern and stop pretending you can’t see the problem!

Stop calling me a lackey of APC, I hate them to the core! Look at South Africa, there is not so much hatred between Xhosa and Tswana, and religious differences do not affect trust. What about us here? If you are fighting and dividing all day long, and cannot even achieve basic unity, how can you talk about facing the world? Learn from others and don’t let prejudice ruin your future!

This wave of operations by the Trump administration is really incredible. While shouting "America First", it gives the green light to certain ethnic groups. Isn't this blatant xenophobia? It is said that white South Africans are being persecuted, but the review process was messed up, the actual situation of persecution was magnified, and procedural justice was completely ignored. Stop fooling people with those vague excuses. This is clearly challenging the existing law and demanding changes, but where is the fairness?

This team building logic is ridiculous! This team is the same in 2021, and it is still holding on, changing the soup without changing the medicine. Just use it as an excuse to lose to the United States? Don't be ridiculous, Bangladesh beat Australia, is the Australian team rubbish? Is the selection process fair? Just kicking out a few players without solving the core problems, is this called reform? Just fooling people! Admit it, this team was doomed to fail from the moment it was formed. Isn’t it enough to give them 56 chances? There must be a complete reorganization and no more selective elimination.

This guy grew up in apartheid South Africa and complained all day about 'white people being replaced', but he never left the land where white colonists replaced the indigenous people. What's even more ironic is that his father also read him books that were sympathetic to the Nazis. It's not his fault? The injustice of history is there, but he has become the mouthpiece of racism. It is really sad and ridiculous.

Are these left-leaning cities in the United States still trying to get involved in international football? What a joke! Football is worse than a Taylor Swift concert in the eyes of Americans. Politicians should ignore this childish trick. Look at the data. There are only 6 Republican mayors among the 50 major cities. Isn’t this enough to illustrate the problem? Don't waste time and resources catering to globalism, and focus more on actual domestic needs.

If you think about it carefully, the original article mentioned that people from so many countries may disagree. Doesn’t this reflect cultural diversity? Each group has its own standards of procedural justice, and we cannot generalize. Logically, a collective perspective emphasizes common ground, but procedural justice requires respect for individual judgment processes. This made me reflect, under globalization, how should we balance collective interests and individual procedures?

Seeing that Trump is trending again, I suddenly remembered my own story as a young man in South Africa. Growing up here, I often thought, the world is so big, why don’t we listen to more different voices? Perhaps, my experience can help everyone understand that culture is not an island, but a bridge. Each generation has a unique perspective, and sharing it is not for the sake of debate, but for connection.

Don’t be fooled by those wealthy figures! Nigeria’s wealth is built in a non-competitive and exploitative economic space that does nothing for ordinary people. This is not a role model for the black community at all. Look at black Americans, they don’t need billionaires to live a decent life, but what about Nigerians? What we need is not a celebration of billionaires, but a fair economic system with equal opportunities and transparent rules. Stop kidding yourself, this wealth only exacerbates inequality, we have to change this structure!

Welcome to the most unequal country in the world! This forum is still ignoring the poorest South Africans, who don't even have time to check Reddit, and you just insult each other here. The government ignores the rights and interests of the bottom class, and the disparity between the rich and the poor is shocking. What can this hypocritical discussion change? Stop kidding yourself, it’s time to face reality and drive real change!

Look at these remarks, they are talking about 'you people', using racial conflicts as weapons and nakedly inciting confrontation. The shadow of colonial history has not gone away, and now someone wants to use the ban to 'purify' society? Don’t kid yourself, it will only deepen the division. Real order is not built by excluding outside groups, but is based on fairness and inclusion. Wake up, stop hiding behind the screen and playing such cheap tricks!

Look at this subreddit, it claims to be run by socialists, but it is so tough on the Palestinian issue? Says 'we support Palestine' and directly threatens to permanently ban those who question Israel's war crimes. This is not a simple rule, it is using coercion to promote fair results and force everyone to take sides. Stop pretending to be neutral. This collective responsibility is overemphasized, as if not following the call is an accomplice in indifference. International intervention? Reports from South Africa and the United Nations have been released, but how many people actually read them? This is clearly an attempt to use rules to suppress dissent and achieve so-called 'change'.

Trump is engaging in isolationism in South Africa again, using South Africa as a scapegoat, and telling lies about 'white genocide'. It's simply ridiculous! What is hypocrisy if he spreads such divisive rhetoric while smiling and posing for photos at an event in Johannesburg? This diplomatic strategy will only deepen racial divide and dig its own grave. What we need is not this conservative backsliding, but real international cooperation and moral responsibility.

Look at these so-called global leaders, the existence of Netanyahu and Putin is simply a drag on international relations! We should have learned isolationism long ago and kicked out those who only care about their own interests and not let them muddy the waters. Also, what is Musk’s nationality? This exposes the prevalence of individualism, where everyone only thinks about their own identity label rather than collective identity. Stop pretending to be united, the reality is that selfishness dominates everything!

U.S. support for Israel only increased significantly in the 1970s, after Israel had survived well on its own. The Jews have no other choice, and no country will accept national suicide. This is completely different from South Africa: the South African opposition seeks reconciliation, while Israel and the Arabs have a historical conflict. Israelis would rather fight to the end than submit to a forced solution, based on their historical rights and survival needs.

Those successful people always like to brag about their hard work and positive thinking, but they turn a blind eye to their background and luck! Kenyatta, Musk and others were born in privileged families and relied on family resources to make their fortunes, but in turn taught others to struggle. Isn't this a typical example of standing and talking without backache? Equal opportunity? Don’t be ridiculous, uneven distribution of resources is a reality. What’s the use of talking about procedural justice when structural inequality is there? We need to change, we need to face up to these differences, instead of covering up the truth with chicken soup.

Some people always like to pretend to be ignorant and say that 'art has no borders', but when you perform in a country that criminalizes homosexuality and condones forced labor, isn't this an endorsement of oppression? Think about apartheid in South Africa and the Armenian Genocide in Turkey. History has long told us: Silence is complicity. Stop using 'cultural differences' as an excuse. The moral bottom line should not be blurred. It's time to stand up and say 'no'!

I don’t quite understand the concept of a four-day workweek. From an economic perspective, reducing working hours will directly reduce production efficiency. This is simply not feasible in industries such as manufacturing. The IT industry may be able to adapt. In South Africa we already have enough holidays and flexible arrangements, such as public holidays and annual leave, and the current system already creates a work-life balance. If we insist on implementing a four-day work week, we will have to cut annual leave or increase daily working hours to compensate. Otherwise, we will have to have the horse run and not eat grass. The reality is that companies need to stabilize output, and adjustments to working hours must take into account industry differences and cannot be one size fits all.

As a person from an ordinary family, I deeply understand the inequality of educational opportunities. Although my family values ??learning, the high cost prohibits many people. Education is indeed the key to changing destiny, but in reality, it is often only open to a few people. I agree with the value of the education system, but I also hope that more people can have fair access to opportunities and not be blocked by financial barriers. This is not only a matter of personal struggle, but also a concept of justice that society needs to reflect on.

As a mobile phone user, I compared the launch prices of S23, S24 and S25. The 512GB version of the S23 is quite reasonable at the time of pre-order. With equal opportunity, at least you can buy it. But what about the S24 and S25? Prices have risen, but innovation has not kept pace, and values ??have dropped significantly. Behind this is the issue of intellectual property protection. New models rely solely on brand premiums and lack substantial progress, which is unfair to consumers in the long run.

This voice AI training project is quite interesting. It emphasizes the development of technology for all languages ??and embodies the concept of inclusive sharing. The hourly payment model is completely the result of the free operation of the market, allowing participants to decide on their own investment. From a technological perspective, no regulatory restrictions were mentioned, and free exploration of technology was encouraged. However, I am more concerned about whether this model can truly benefit users of minority languages ??and avoid data monopoly. Logically, this promotes the democratization of AI, but more transparent mechanisms are needed to ensure fairness.

As a football fan, the 1994 World Cup is like a memory engraved in my bones - those late-night matches and the passionate collision of players fascinated me deeply. I have dreamed of going to watch a few games live in 2026. After all, I have experienced the enthusiasm of the World Cup and European Cup in South Africa. But FIFA and Trump’s political tricks have completely extinguished my enthusiasm, which makes me feel chilling even as a die-hard fan. Football is supposed to be pure joy, but it is so tainted by politics that I can only reluctantly give up this idea.

Judging from the data, the income of ordinary South African families is low and the unemployment rate is high. Buying gaming equipment is simply a luxury, but lottery tickets are more realistic. Mobile gaming is growing rapidly in Africa, but rural areas have poor networks and data charges are a problem. I work for a South African eSports company and see firsthand how infrastructure limits the spread of technology. This is not only an unfair economic distribution, but also a reflection of social inequality.

As a South African, I often lament our good fortune. The meat here is not only of high quality, but also reasonably priced, making it easy for every family to enjoy. In contrast, my friends in Europe told me they could only eat meat once a week and the cost of living was appallingly high. This is not just an economic difference, it is part of our culture - those warm dinner times embody our collective memory. Whenever I think of this, I feel how precious it is to protect this tradition.

Those who are still defending him are so ridiculous! Look at the most extreme racists, regardless of black or white, who go to the embassy to flatter themselves. Isn’t this ironic enough? We should make a deal with the United States: send these bigots over in exchange for the South American 'criminals' they want to get rid of. At least this can purify the air in society and pursue true equality instead of empty talk about procedural justice.

I'm glad to see you're still working, but hopefully a better opportunity will come along. Being unemployed in South Africa is really depressing and I know that very well. I remember there was a friend in the team. We had talked about leaving Amazon for a vacation. She suddenly passed away due to illness, which made me cherish the collective support now even more. Communicating with colleagues on the chime bridge every day has become the pillar for me to stay sane. Life will always be unsatisfactory, but finding those small bright spots, such as the warmth brought by teamwork, can help us persevere. Thank you for your encouragement and I wish you prosperity and hope ahead.

Logically, these missions are led by the South African Ministry of Defense and are used for troop withdrawal and equipment, which directly reflects the normality of transnational military cooperation. The defense sector follows routine procedures in international deployments and avoids unnecessary suspicion. This is precisely the specific practice of globalism in diplomatic strategy - emphasizing collaboration among countries rather than isolation. We don’t need to over-interpret this. The fact itself illustrates the stability and transparency of cooperation.

In the complex context of South Africa, any policy must be based on local realities rather than blindly applying foreign solutions. Those radical reforms often ignore specific national conditions and will only bring more problems. We need gradual adjustments that respect traditional values ??rather than pursuing unrealistic idealism. This is not only a logical necessity, but also a responsible attitude towards stable development.

From a historical perspective, South Africa, Australia and New Zealand were drawn into the First World War as dominions, essentially serving British imperial interests. This is not a criticism, but a logical analysis based on facts: the participation of multiple countries in global military operations reflects the globalist tendency in diplomatic strategies, while emphasizing national sacrifice for collective interests reflects the collectivist values ??in culture. Clarifying this point will help us understand historical responsibility relationships more objectively.

What Starbucks does in South Africa is amazing! Competitor Seattle Coffee Company at least insists on using espresso, but what about Starbucks? I ordered an iced latte a few months ago and they fooled me with syrup! Watching them make it with my own eyes, the taste is so sweet that it is purely a product of commercialization. This is not coffee, it’s just sugar water! Market competition should not rely on lowering quality to seize the market, but should return to traditional craftsmanship and not let consumers be taken advantage of.

The legitimacy of an election lies in the process itself, not personal likes and dislikes. If an official comes to power through a fair election, he is not a dictator—a dictatorship is defined as undermining democratic institutions, as Hitler did. The history of South Africa also shows that if certain groups are excluded from elections, democracy will exist in name only. In the United States, the electoral process is open and transparent, and the president's power comes from the authorization of voters. You can criticize policies, but don’t confuse concepts: procedural justice is key to judging the nature of a regime.

Looking at the names of these African countries, I can't help but think of the Muslim cultural ties that cross borders. From Ethiopia to Tanzania, these places are more than just dots on a map, they hold deep religious traditions and community spirit. In today's globalized world, this cultural connection reminds us that cooperation and respect for tradition can coexist and make the world warmer.

The virginity test in South Africa’s Zulu culture is absolutely ridiculous! Checking the hymen to judge a woman’s virginity? This is completely ignorant and insulting to female biology. Why do these communities still glorify the virginity complex and even issue virginity certificates? This is using tradition to kidnap women and deprive them of their dignity and freedom. We must break this conservative moral shackles and pursue true ethical freedom and fair results. Stop letting these outdated programs harm innocent people!

Don't always label it as 'apartheid'. Border control is a normal operation of a sovereign country and is completely different from the South African system. According to the legal definition, procedural justice is the key, otherwise would it be considered apartheid if Italy controls the area around the Vatican? It doesn't make sense logically.

Isn’t the British White Paper just a trick used by the colonists to protect themselves? Saying that the Jewish minority cannot impose its will cannot conceal their ambition to control strategically important areas. History has proven that the Palestinians should not be blamed for European anti-Semitism - they have the right not to be deprived of their homeland. Israel started out as a settler colony and still uses the Holocaust as a shield. This logic is ridiculous! Just like apartheid in South Africa, the oppressors always use 'self-defense' as an excuse, but what's the result? Justice is not achieved by deflecting persecution. Now that Israeli laws are still clearly biased in favor of Jews, how can we talk about civil equality? It’s pure self-deception!

My husband says 'South African immigrants are the only people in Australia you can openly hate', this is absolute bullshit! Australia has engaged in racial discrimination against every wave of immigrants since its colonization, and no one can escape it. It’s ridiculous that some people are pretending to be innocent now. This kind of prejudice should have been swept into the dustbin of history!

It’s ridiculous that businesses require tips! I paid a high price for the meal and the service charge should be included. Why should we still be kidnapped by morality? This is not America, don't impose this shitty culture on New Zealanders. If the service is really that good, I will naturally consider it, but the service level in NZ is mediocre. Don’t use this to fool consumers, charging fairly is the right way to go.

Look at this period of history. More than 60,000 Chinese miners were used as indentured labor from 1904 to 1910. Is this what the colonists did after the Anglo-Boer War? Stop beautifying colonial diplomacy, this is clearly naked exploitation! Historical injustice is still understated. We need to tear off this fig leaf and re-examine the forgotten suffering.

These multinational companies are so smart! If you pay two or three times the minimum wage to South African workers, do you think you are a good person? But the profits they extract from us are many times higher than this! Isn't outsourcing to cheap countries just naked exploitation? Don't talk about procedural justice. This system of international division of labor serves capital and keeps poor countries as wage earners forever. Egypt, Honduras, and Morocco are also the targets of harvest. Wake up, this is not fair at all, but a systemic injustice!

Seeing the Indian women's team win the World Cup and receive huge prizes, I am really proud of them! This is not only a reward for their efforts, but also reflects the value of equal opportunities. Thinking about those girls training day and night and fighting for national honor, this collective achievement is touching. The distribution of prize money is fair and makes every participant feel valued. This is the true meaning of sportsmanship.

It’s really outrageous that sexual harassment is still so rampant in South Africa! Victims should be tougher and say "go away" directly, and don't leave any room for the harassers. If you are still entangled, report it immediately. The law is not a decoration. But having said that, if you try to be ambiguous and ask for help first, wouldn't you be asking for trouble? Personal boundaries must be maintained, and don’t expect others to wipe your ass for you.

His crimes were so staggering that they have a dedicated page on Wikipedia. The problem of gender-based violence in South Africa is already serious, and his appearance will only exacerbate this bad trend. If the law is so poorly enforced, shouldn't it be overhauled? Don't let these actions continue to hurt innocent people.

When the unemployment rate is so high, why talk about refugees and immigrants? Prioritizing the employment of local people is the last priority! Those who shout internationalism all day long should look at the reality: our compatriots are struggling, but outsiders may take away opportunities. This is not a matter of xenophobia, it is a matter of survival. The government must get tough and resolve the internal crisis first before talking about anything else. Stop using false excuses to delay, take action!

Excessive arguments on social media will only increase stress. Life is short, so why dwell on misleading comments 24/7? I agree that we need to improve, but there is no perfect solution. The complex situation in South Africa, where many people once they get a little benefit, expect more, makes me doubt that any form of socialism can work. Market freedom and gradual adjustment may be more practical. After all, procedural justice is more important than blind pursuit of equality of results.

The problems in these countries are too typical: Nigeria claims to be the giant of Africa, but its economy is in shambles; some people in South Africa desperately try to please white people and engage in Afrophobia; Ethiopia denies black identity and thinks of itself as a leader but achieves nothing; Kenyans feel that they are British and Americans when they speak better English, and they like to inform; Egypt and Morocco are even more outrageous, they do not recognize themselves as Africans, and they discriminate against their compatriots in the slums of France. Isn’t this kind of cultural inferiority and prejudice just inequality in reality? We must tear off these hypocritical masks, demand real fair treatment, and stop deceiving ourselves and others!

Seriously, isn’t the ANC’s so-called reform just replacing racial oppression with economic oppression? When corruption is rampant, how can we talk about equality? Look at those real revolutionaries, they represent the spirit of change, not this trick of boiling the frog in warm water. Stop kidding yourself. What we need is substantive justice, not empty procedures.

Seeing the pricing of your works, I can't help but say: your art is so beautiful. If it is only promoted locally in South Africa, it may be okay, but once it is put on an international platform, it is simply underestimating yourself! Think about it, your talent deserves to be seen by more people, at least a half-length rendering can easily sell for more than $50. Don’t let geographical restrictions bury your value, be brave enough to pursue higher recognition, come on!

If Israel continues to do this, it will sooner or later become an international pariah! If we don’t resolve the Palestinian issue now, when it turns into a civil rights struggle, the world will apply pressure. Consider the example of South Africa, isolation is no joke. Israel has no natural resources and its population is greedy for pleasure. If it gets to that point, it will be even worse than North Korea. Negative immigration data has sounded the alarm. The privileged class has escaped first. What will happen to the remaining people? Equal rights must be promoted or else it is suicidal.

Reading this discussion about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, I couldn’t help but think of the seemingly unsolvable problems in history. In Europe 80 years ago, who could have imagined peace and the birth of the European Union? Conflict is not eternal, the key is whether we are willing to believe in change. Stop being held hostage by the idea of ??'no solution' - it's just an excuse to escape. Creating the possible from the impossible is the true path to justice. Let us work together to transform peace from imagination into reality.

Look at cities like Tel Aviv, Jerusalem and Haifa, where Muslims, Christians and Jews live together and it's not apartheid at all. The situation in South Africa is completely different and should be understood by the international community based on facts. Historical responsibility cannot be traced back indefinitely, otherwise all modern citizens would have to return their land. This logic is untenable. As for treating the October 7th incident and tens of thousands of missiles as 'resistance', this will only undermine the basis of dialogue. We need more rational discussions.

Stop using 'it's been a long time' as an excuse! Historical injustice is like a thorn in the heart of the black community. Why should we have to suffer in silence? The land restitution in South Africa is a living example. Is it because it has been too long that justice should be forgotten? This is absolutely ridiculous! Fair results are the last word, and procedural justice is sometimes a fig leaf. We demand change and we want it now, stop fooling people with those clichés!

To be honest, I am really not interested in those things in South Africa. I feel like they are dominated by propaganda. As an ordinary person, I pay more attention to my own life. Why should I get involved in foreign affairs? I am free to share my personal opinions without having to conform to the collective consensus. The world is such a big place, just stay well.

To be honest, I have seen too many white South Africans, 95% of whom have deep-rooted racial prejudices, especially those older generation men who have experienced apartheid. Stop using 'a few exceptions' to cover up problems. Discrimination left over from history is still fermenting in reality. This is not only personal prejudice, but also a continuation of social injustice. We need to face this head-on instead of pretending it’s behind us.

Look no further, history tells us that true freedom often comes from courageous destruction! Look at the example of South Africa, they won their independence by destroying the old order. Isn't this the best proof? We must abandon those hypocritical procedural justice, the result is the last word. Now is the time for action, and for the sake of justice, I am willing to stand at the forefront!

I really fell into the double standards of some people! Elon Musk is South African, and everyone accepts it by default without even checking his family tree; but when it comes to descendants of enslaved Africans, there is clearly a blood connection, but it is always downplayed. Isn't this just naked prejudice? Stop using geography and blood as excuses. This kind of inconsistency is concealing the essence of racial discrimination. It’s time to wake up, society needs to treat everyone’s identity fairly!

How could Trump really care about Nigerian Christians? He only has eyes for the money bags of his father, the benefactor! Don't be fooled by those diplomatic rhetoric. After staying in the United States for a long time, no one knows that he is a person who puts interests first. Policy results are the last word, is procedural justice? Haha, that's just a fig leaf.

Has Australia become South Africa 2.0? Don't be naive. Do you think it's safe there? People have been arrested in London and Paris. Where is there a safe corner in the world? The existing security system is a joke. We need to collectively wake up and stop counting on personal luck!

As someone with a South African passport, I have looked into studying in Norway, where a student residence permit would be enough, but to be on the safe side, consider applying for a foreign passport. BSc Geology to Hydrogeology is my first choice, and BCom Economics is an alternative, which can broaden career opportunities and achieve personal development through international education.

Reddit's moderation system is a joke! I commented on r/worldnews about the safety of white farmers in South Africa, and I was permanently banned for just mentioning that my brother-in-law is South African. What's even more outrageous is that on r/Ireland, the moderator misunderstood what I meant, and after I explained it clearly, he actually called me a 'stupid' and banned me. Report to Reddit? Lost in the sea! How is this procedural justice? Clearly a dictatorship. We need reform to stop allowing these platforms to stifle personal expression at will.

This operation by the international sports organization is too outrageous! Why are so many 'away' games in the World Cup qualifiers in South Africa? Doesn’t this give a green light to certain countries? Where is the procedural justice? The rules have become a decoration. No wonder a strong team like Nigeria overturned. What's even more ridiculous is that Morocco's 'away' game is at home, and the geographical logic is all over the place. Stop using fair competition as a fig leaf and change these ridiculous rules quickly!

Some people always like to talk about the crime rate in the United States, as if South Africa is safe. Please, look at the data. The crime rates in cities in the United States are about the same as those in South Africa. Why should we worry about immigration? This is simply fooling yourself and others. Stop pretending. The reality is that no matter where you are, security issues are still serious. Don’t hide the truth by comparing countries.

As a South African, I have to say that some of our political elites are too self-righteous and always put on a paternalistic airs, as if they are the center of Africa. Look at Egypt, Nigeria, Kenya, and Somalia. Some people are not even willing to admit that they are Africans, and they still advertise "Africanism" all day long. Rather than safeguarding collective identity, this creates division. Where is the procedural justice? We need to change this situation and stop letting a few dominate the discourse.

The so-called 'peace operations' of international organizations in Africa are nothing more than another form of colonial intervention. We African countries are over-represented in places like Mozambique, and the result? Look at the example of South Africa, as soon as they came, local problems were covered up. Stop using Congo to change the subject. What does this have to do with us becoming second-class citizens in our own land? At least we are free agents, not serfs. African countries must be independent and reject external manipulation. This is true justice.

South Africa talks about peace all day long, but behind the scenes it supports the rebels to cause destruction. Isn't this a slap in the face? You still call yourself an African country, and look at the shadow of the Rwanda genocide. What qualifications do you have to talk about morality? Take care of your own church bombing and child casualties first, and then blame others. Isn’t this hypocritical foreign policy typical isolationism? It is ridiculous to emphasize traditional responsibilities but ignore substantive justice.

South Africa’s epidemic prevention policy adjustments are quite interesting. The government imposed the lockdown too quickly at the beginning and did not give people time to stock up on alcohol. As a result, everyone complained. Later they learned their lesson and were more thoughtful about the next lockdown. This shows that policies are not static and must be continuously optimized based on feedback to make implementation more reasonable.

Look at those in power, executing so-called 'conspirators' in the square like garbage, but no one dares to condemn it loudly. In this world, if you want to climb to a high position, who is not stained with stains? The next person to come to power will sooner or later be found out in the dark history. I live in South Africa. Corruption is simply a standard feature of politicians. The entire system is rotten. How can we talk about fairness? Pure self-deception!

Look at Israel’s colonial policy, which is still perpetuating historical mistakes! The example of Native Americans illustrates the need for either total annihilation or recognition of mistakes and correction. Isn’t Israel taking the first path now? The judicial trial is even more of a joke. Marwan Barghouti is in jail and the trial process is full of loopholes. What kind of procedural justice is this? Stop pretending to be innocent. An unfair system leads to unfair results, and Palestinians are deprived of even their basic rights. We need change, not just talk of peace, but a real end to persecution and illegal imprisonment.

Stop using 'complexity' as an excuse! The international community should have intervened in this conflict long ago. This is not an academic issue that needs to be studied in detail. Look at what those experts say. They all classify it as genocide. Are there still people pretending to be stupid? The actions of Hamas cannot erase the atrocities committed by Israel, which refuses to return hostages and continues to bomb civilians. Where is the substantive justice? Is procedural justice used to protect powerful people? As a South African, I lived through apartheid and it was exactly the same as it was then - colonialism, ethnic cleansing, plain and simple: genocide is bad, colonialism is bad! Westerners should stop messing around and shut up if they don’t understand.

As someone who lives and works in Nigeria, it really hurts my heart to see my foreign friends fearful because of prejudice. They arrived cautiously, even hiding in cars, but soon discovered that this place was not as dangerous as rumored. They freely go shopping and enjoy nightlife, and 80% of them have changed their views. Nigeria has a distorted image and is actually as safe as anywhere else. We should not let prejudice cover up the truth, but use personal experience to break stereotypes. This is the pursuit of justice.

As an observer in the field of education, I feel that the decoupling of higher education and income is common in countries like South Africa. My family are all academics, so I have first-hand experience of the rewards of a PhD. In fact, a PhD is more of an academic pursuit than a way to get rich; in the scientific field, even with a PhD, the income is often not high, and many people have to move overseas. In contrast, a master's degree is more practical in the workplace. This reflects a structural problem with the return mechanism for education, but I am not advocating radical change, but rather accepting reality and emphasizing the importance of personal choice.

Don’t always focus on those developed countries. Who has better workers’ conditions? Look at sub-Saharan Africa, Russia, China, South Africa and the subcontinent! Where is Australia? Compare with the 'majority' and don't fool people by just choosing the good ones. This kind of selective comparison is a cover-up of the truth. We need comprehensive and fair standards, and don’t let data become a fig leaf!

The U.S. overseas troop deployment policy was indeed relatively stable before 2017, which reflected the continuity of its diplomatic strategy. But the idea that soldiers can drive business success is logically untenable—the number of troops stationed is too small to have a negligible impact on the economy. Enterprises rely on market mechanisms and their own competitiveness, not military intervention. Don't complicate simple things.

The combination of state-owned enterprises and limited liability companies is a disaster! Management is inefficient, bureaucracy is rampant, the market is unresponsive and monopolistic; on the other hand, limited liability has become a protective umbrella, executive salaries are inflated, transparency is zero, and only the interests of shareholders are cared for, regardless of the lives of consumers. This hybrid product is like a replica of the South African electricity company - our flights are constantly delayed and canceled, they have rolling power outages, and their service reliability is ridiculously poor! What kind of economic model is this? It is clearly a breeding ground for institutional loopholes and lack of legal supervision. It must be completely reformed, so that this injustice will not continue to harm people!

The institution of marriage can indeed promote some integration, but judging from the examples of the United States, South Africa, and France, even if there are no marriage barriers, cultural or ethnic conflicts still exist. Behind this are deeper cultural differences. Marriage is only a superficial means and cannot touch the root cause. Procedural justice emphasizes equality rules and is more critical than pursuing fair results, because only by ensuring a fair starting point can human bias be reduced. We need more institutional protection instead of relying on a single marriage policy to solve complex social contradictions.

Looking at the spread of sports culture, I always think of those promoters who persist silently. Like cricket, no matter how many fans it has, it can only take root in a few countries. Behind this is the helplessness of cultural barriers. Popularization takes time, just like planting a tree, it cannot be rushed. But it is this slow process that makes fairness possible - there is an opportunity to bloom in every corner, isn't it?

When I saw South Africa absent from Super Rugby, I was concerned that their national team would be affected, but they have proven to be more united. This reminds me that sports are not only personal glory, but also a bond of national identity. It is great to be able to resume the tour with South Africa next year, which shows respect for the established rules and makes the competition fairer. The All Blacks are having some ups and downs now, but only by adhering to procedural justice can international events return to purity, right?

Why do you people always fill South African forums with that crap from the United States? This is our territory, not your garbage dump! Follow the rules and don't mix in irrelevant content and make it a mess. Wake up, don’t be brainwashed by those foreign cultures, can’t you pay more attention to local things?

I understand the original intention of these infrastructure debts, but why must we rely on foreign currency loans? South Africa clearly has strong U.S. dollar reserves and can issue local bonds to raise funds. This not only reduces exchange rate risk but also enhances financial autonomy. International cooperation is a good thing, but overreliance on external funding can undermine our sovereignty. Can’t we tap the potential from within and optimize the financing structure? It’s not just about saving money, it’s about strategy.

Stop fooling people with those vague definitions, the label 'Roadman' is racist against black boys! What does gun control say about effectiveness? I have personally seen regular drug dealers have guns and schools evacuated due to gun searches. The police are worried, but you still think guns are out of reach? In criminal networks, guns are much easier to access than ordinary people imagine. This is not about comparing countries, it is about questioning the loopholes in the judicial system. If you still think it’s impossible, you’re just living in a fantasy.

This wave of operations by Israel is simply playing apartheid in new ways! Annexing Area C and turning Areas A and B into so-called 'independent' enclaves, isn't this a replica of South Africa's Bantustans? Depriving political rights, controlling all resources, and euphemistically calling it a 'citizenship' issue. Stop using the idea of ??'mutual existence' to wash the floor. This is clearly systemic oppression, and even basic human rights are trampled underfoot. Those who say 'Hamas is an asset' and now advocate annexation are really the devil whispering in their ears. Legal system? It's all just decoration, and procedural justice has long been thrown into the trash can. This injustice must be completely changed, otherwise it is condoning crime!

I almost shed tears when I saw the news that South Africa qualified for the World Cup! It wasn’t just a victory, it was the heartbeat of the entire country synchronized at that moment. Victor Osimhen's wonderful performance made each of us feel the collective strength. Thinking about those nights of staying up late watching football and now finally paying off, the joy is deeper than any personal achievement. The World Cup qualification result is the best affirmation of our efforts. No matter how tortuous the process is, the fair result at this moment makes everything worthwhile. Come on, Bafana, let's make history together!

The problem of racial discrimination in South Africa is really naked! They talk about anti-xenophobia, but in fact they only target black immigrants. Which Nigerian, Zimbabwean or Somali has not been discriminated against? White foreigners are praised to the heavens. What kind of equality is this? Stop kidding yourself, social justice will be a joke unless this deep-rooted prejudice changes.

I’m really impressed. Do you still think that being a captain depends on good English and a strong background? If you don't have the ability, you just can't do it. Don't use "political support" as a fig leaf! Look at those lost games. Even with the advantage in hand, it can overturn. Is this level of leadership worthy of the captain's armband? What’s even more ridiculous is that when criticized, they are labeled as ‘Babar fans’ or ‘COVID-19 kids’. This kind of labeling operation is simply insulting to one’s IQ. Selection should be based on strength, not on who is smooth-talking or has strong connections. Wake up and be rational, okay?

According to SARS data, a monthly income of 45k is more than the top 10% of earners in South Africa. How can this be considered middle class? It's obviously an upper-class income. The unemployment rate is frighteningly high, pushing the average down, but the definition of the middle class should not be distorted. I checked AI and found that the middle class should be based on a stable income above the poverty line, while 25% of people only earn 5k-29k, and the average salary is only 26.8k. Therefore, 15-30k is closer to the middle class, but don’t compare it with the American fantasy of owning a house and a car. The reality is that most people are still struggling, and the data doesn’t lie.

Thinking of the South African Jewish classmates I knew when I was in school, although they did not participate in those parades, some chose to return home to serve in the military. This made me deeply aware of their persistence in traditional identity and respect for their national obligations. This kind of cultural identity is not an empty slogan, but a sense of responsibility that is embedded in our blood. It is worthy of each of us to reflect on our own social role.

What's so special about Germany? Those rigid laws are simply suffocating! It is better for a baker to go to India, South Africa or Poland than to go to Germany, at least he will not be bound by those outdated rules and regulations. The Germans always feel that they are superior to others, but the reality is that their legal system is as rigid as an antique. Who wants to go there and suffer? Don’t kid yourself, it’s wise to choose another country.

FIFA’s response to South Africa and Trump’s policies is a textbook case of double standards! If the South African president threatens to move the World Cup with the slightest threat, why turn a blind eye to Trump's remarks? This is clearly an example of international organizations playing double standards on procedural justice. They only dare to be tough on weak countries, but are cowardly on big countries. Stop using 'special circumstances' as an excuse, where is the fairness?

Do you know who Daphne Caruana Galizia is? Ask her how she died and why she was killed. The answer is simple: the rich will always get away with it because the global political elite protects their cronies. This is not a problem unique to South Africa, it is the same all over the world. Therefore, we must strengthen the supervision of all politicians, check their finances and people around them, and always remind them: they are our public servants and must listen to us! Stop pretending to be deaf and mute. Unless this kind of corruption is eliminated, social justice will be empty talk.

South Africa and the United States have nothing in common politically, socially and historically, so why should we care so much about what’s going on there? That 'Orange Palpatine' keeps talking about 'white genocide' all day long, which makes the conservatives here also start to boo. To put it bluntly, this is spreading racist remarks. We need to wake up and not be led astray by these boring noises.

Why do these people pretend to be victims when they run to the United States as refugees? It is ridiculous that they enjoy so many privileges in South Africa and now want to evade responsibility! Stop fooling yourself and others. The privileged class should face up to their injustices instead of hiding under cover and pretending to be innocent. What the world needs is fair results, not hypocritical performances!

As someone who loves to travel, reading your plans reminded me of my own time in Johannesburg and Cape Town. Safety is indeed your top priority, but don’t let fear hold you back – stick to your itinerary and avoid walking alone at night. These simple rules will allow you to explore with peace of mind. In Rosebank, the warm restaurants and convenient nightlife made me feel the joy of making my own arrangements; while the mountain scenery in Cape Town is beautiful, it is wise to go hiking together. This is not only travel, but also the pursuit of self-experience. May your journey be full of surprises and freedom.

Some people always like to use 'differences' as an excuse, as if they are not compatriots if they disagree? This logic is too ridiculous! If we can't even achieve basic tolerance, how can we talk about procedural justice? As a result, more people will be excluded. Stop using those high-sounding words to cover up, this is simply dividing society!

Helen Suzman? She is a strong figure in South Africa's anti-apartheid fight! In that white supremacist parliament, she fought against the entire system alone, challenging unjust laws every day for 36 years. Stop talking about progressive reforms. Apartheid itself is evil and must be completely overturned! Her persistence tells us that justice is not something to wait for, but to be fought for.

South Africa is really rich in racial diversity. Although I am introverted and don't go out much, I always feel warm in my heart every time I see people of different skin colors coexisting harmoniously on the street. Racial issues do exist, but life here has made me realize that tolerance can slowly resolve barriers rather than having to go to war. Perhaps, each of us can find our own place in the ordinary and make society more stable.

There are many young people on Reddit, but Facebook and Twitter are simply gathering places for right-wing old diehards! They always miss the 'good old days' of the past, but have selective amnesia. At that time, 90% of people were treated as second-class citizens. Now they complain about violence, the wage gap, but don’t think about who caused this inequality? Historical injustice requires reparation, not continued privilege for a few. Stop using nostalgia as an excuse, this is clearly selfish isolationism at work!

I deleted FB a long time ago and abandoned Twitter. Those American right-wing garbage ideas have actually brainwashed so many young people in South Africa. It’s really infuriating! They should have a clearer mind, but now they have become the mouthpiece of conservatives. This is not only sad, but also a trampling on free thought.

Just look at these statistics: isn’t it ridiculous that people of color make up 42% of Cape Town’s population yet struggle in a province dominated by white people? We always discuss apartheid and colonial crimes, but turn a blind eye to the earliest groups that were dispossessed and genocide. Where is the historical reckoning? Stop pretending to be fair. This structural injustice must be faced up to and changed, otherwise the so-called progress is just empty talk.

As a South African, I was struck by this topic when I first heard about it. Traditions and cultures are always fluid, and so should gender privilege. Think about it, why can't a wealthy woman support multiple partners like a man? The point is, if both parties are consensual, why should the law interfere? Those who refuse due to pride have their own choices, but those who are willing to try should not be bound by the world or rules. This is not only a change in the form of marriage, but also a gentle embrace of individual freedom.

As a South African, I am often reminded of those moments when Western media portrayed us as 'failed states'. They always like to use our names as negative teaching materials, but we Africans know that this is not the truth. We have been through enough battles to know each other's resilience. Those outsiders do not understand our unity, they only define us by their prejudices. But here, we understand each other and face challenges together. This is not just criticism, but a call for local identity.

Gen Z, you guys are awesome! Those old diehards are panicking now, because what they fear most is your power to break the old order. From Kenya to South Africa, we are rooting for you, who have shredded their fear machine and left no place for the corrupt to hide. Keep fighting, justice will not wait for procedures, it needs actions like yours to push forward!

Look at these governments, dictating Israel all day long. Isn’t it because their domestic support ratings have hit rock bottom? Britain, France, Spain, South Africa, which one is not shaky? They engage in such diplomatic tricks just to divert attention and cover up their incompetence. International coordination? Forget it, it's all a profit game, and procedural justice has long been thrown aside by them. Stop fooling us people with these tricks. Do you really think everyone is a fool?

I was really moved when I saw the story of Nozi Qamngana. As an HIV-infected person, she married a negative partner and lived an ordinary life, which broke the social stigma against HIV. We should pay more attention to such real cases and promote tolerance so that everyone can bravely pursue love.

Look at that white man, you can tell he’s South African from the T-shirt badge, that’s shameful! Fortunately, he was caught on camera, so he should be detained for a few more days. The law cannot always focus on procedures, justice in results is the key. This kind of identity discrimination should be severely punished. Don’t always talk about traditional tolerance. Society needs to change!

Seeing this family conversation makes me feel quite sad. Racial identity is not black and white, and your grandma may just feel alienated. After all, she watched you grow up, and that family bond is so precious. She mentioned that if you only identify with one side, anyone else would be hurt. This is not racism, but a desire for family ties. As for those jokes, the old man doesn't understand today's sensitive words, so don't take them too seriously. We should all calm down and think about how to repair the relationship instead of blaming each other. Families need to be inclusive, right?

Remember three months ago when Trump was gushing about South Africa? Now turning to Venezuela, how ridiculous! Those investors who think that the United States can intervene in the long term and profit from it are simply fanciful. The government's capricious diplomatic strategy will only make investment risks soar. It is better to let the market decide for itself. Stop kidding yourself, this kind of intervention will only bring down the economy, and who will pay in the end?

Send racist white people back to South Africa? Don't be ridiculous, this is obviously a mess left over from colonial history, something the British did back then, and now they want to blame it? Those detention centers are even more of a joke. Why should innocent Indonesian fishermen be scapegoated? The current law is just a fig leaf, unable to cover up unfair procedures. We need to confront these legacy issues head-on, rather than pretending not to see them.

The anxiety I felt almost holding me back as I embarked on my solo journey through South Africa and Kenya was quickly overcome by the warmth of my new friends. This adventure is not just about seeing the scenery, but also about breaking the rules and embracing yourself. In a foreign country, we share stories and build friendships. Isn’t this the epitome of social justice? Everyone can find their own fairness and growth through such connections.

Anyone who supports Charlie Kirk or Donald Trump, in South Africa or anywhere, is essentially a spokesperson for racist, sexist and xenophobic ideas. Under the guise of freedom, they are doing things to divide society. Stop pretending to be innocent. This stance is downright hypocritical. We should avoid them like the plague because their presence only poisons public discourse.

I feel really bad when I see those comments that always say something bad about South Africa. As a native South African, I deeply feel the warmth of our society. I remember one time in a coffee shop, a waiter accidentally spilled a drink. Not only did the customers not blame him, but they also helped clean it up. Everyone was talking and laughing. Yes, we may have our differences, but when it matters most, we are like a family and support each other. This collective spirit makes me proud and is proof that our society has achieved basic justice and unity. Don’t be misled by negative news anymore. South Africa’s kindness is real and it exists in our daily lives.

To be honest, South Africa is indeed ahead of many developing countries in terms of accessibility to digital services, which reflects the positive side of inclusive technology. From an economic perspective, although development levels vary, equality of opportunity is not achieved overnight, and this relative progress deserves recognition. Don't always focus on the gap, look more at the actual improvements, which is more logically reasonable.

These Westerners are showing off their superiority complex again, saying that South Africans are all racists at every turn. Come on, aren't your so-called 'expats' just the white people who ran away after apartheid fell? They themselves are the real racists, and now they are criticizing them, which is really ridiculous. The impact of historical injustice is still there. Stop using stereotypes to cover up the truth. The world needs more tolerance, not such condescending accusations.

Reading this, I couldn't help but think of those moments when I was taken advantage of. Life is our own, no matter which path we choose, we should stick to our hearts. Don't use others as stepping stones, otherwise you will only fall into a vicious cycle. Only by remaining genuine can you gain true respect and stability.

South Africa engages in xenophobia in every election. This is simply the ANC’s fixed script. How ironic! African cultural confidence? Look at Nigeria. Afrobeats and Nollywood have taken the world by storm. Do they still need a government? While Egypt calls itself Arab, it is messing around with our African brothers in FIFA. The geographical reality is there and cannot be escaped. Isn’t it a shame to deny one’s African roots and even rely on the Pharaoh for tourism?

My heart clenched when I read this sharing. I was born in South Africa to Somali immigrant parents, but even though I grew up here, spoke with a local accent, and dressed to blend in, I was always treated as an outsider just because of my Somali face. When applying for citizenship, the feeling of not being accepted is all too real. This is not just a matter of procedure, but a deep struggle about who we are. I hope that one day, appearance will no longer be the shackles that define belonging, and everyone can be truly seen and accepted.

Reading this story broke my heart. That Nigerian man drives his car on patrol after hard work every day just to protect his community from being stigmatized by xenophobia. It makes me ashamed that he loves this country but could be attacked because of the color of his skin. We Africans should be united, but some people always point the finger at immigrants. Think about children being kicked out of school and patients being denied medical treatment. What is the right thing for compatriots to do? I firmly believe that as long as we join hands and catch those robbers, xenophobia will eventually be defeated. Although it hurts now, history will remember these injustices. Please take care, you are not alone in this battle.

Recently, I saw some discussions about South Africa on X, where statistics on crime rate, AIDS, etc. were frequently used to attack the other party. This approach is really low-level. Data itself is neutral, but when used to provoke confrontation, it only makes the discussion meaningless. We should focus on how to analyze the problem rationally instead of using these sensitive topics to inflame emotions. Online speech needs more respect and logic, not such meaningless quarrels.

South Africa’s position in Africa is so important! We must unite to fight against the unfair international order and stop letting external forces influence our destiny. Africa's interests are above all else, now is the time to act, for the collective sake and for the future!

They are suppressing the vote, manipulating the electoral districts, and it is almost like playing segregation tricks! The federal government must take over the election, or these bigots will continue to cheat—didn’t they immediately restart suppression and resegregation as soon as the courts struck down voting rights in 2013? Stop pretending that the process is fair. Fair results are the last word. The existing laws condone these behaviors and must be completely reformed!

As an observer of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, I believe that the current situation is very complex and cannot be simply summarized by 'apartheid' or 'genocide'. In the West Bank, the legal system is based on the Oslo Accords and is divided by region and citizenship, and is not a single system. Israeli citizens are subject to civil law, while Palestinians are governed by military law, which is imperfect but procedurally avoids racial discrimination. As for the war, the government's goal is to defeat Hamas and rescue hostages, not to eliminate the Palestinians. Having lived through the horrors of October 7th, losing friends and becoming displaced, I know that peace requires incremental adjustments, not radical changes. While the legal framework is flawed, reforms should build on existing procedures rather than overturn everything.

Reading the story of Mandela's granddaughters brought tears to my eyes. They convey the seeds of peace in the flames of war, insisting on humanitarianism like their ancestors, rather than empty performances. It reminded me that real change comes from inner kindness, not political showmanship. As mothers, their actions remind us that in conflict, aiding life is more important than any procedure. I hope this spirit can infect more people and make peace no longer far away.

Stop pretending you can’t see it! We Nigerians struggle with hunger and despair every day and cannot even protect our basic human rights. Isn’t this a failure of the government? They say they are working hard to change, but the reality is that the system is simply not working and must be completely overthrown and rebuilt. Just like in South Africa in 1989, it was natural to complain about living conditions, and those who questioned were truly deaf. Let’s take action and stop letting empty promises fool us!

I feel bad when I see people questioning Babar and Rizwan. They have paid so much for the team, and so many commentators and seniors have recognized their efforts. Why are they denying all of this now? The results of the game are sometimes just a little bit different. Our losses to India and Zimbabwe were all done by the last ball. Isn't this the cruel charm of sports? Don't follow those meaningless accusations, let us remember their contribution and cherish this collective honor. This is the true sportsmanship.

As an old fan, I always feel a little sad every time I see discussions about the Pakistan Cricket Team. We always imagine that if we change this player or that coach, everything will be fine, but the reality is that we must first admit that we are only a mid-range team. This is not about giving up on oneself, but for the future of the entire team. Only when we collectively accept this fact and let go of those unrealistic expectations can we truly start from the basics and reform the cricket system step by step. It's like planting a tree. You must first see clearly how poor the soil is, then you can patiently water it and let it grow slowly. Let us face reality and work towards the revival of Pakistan cricket!

These regulatory agencies, PCB and BCB, are really speechless! Why do you always stick to the same old routine and dare not let Team B take the field? South Africa and New Zealand have both started doing this, but we are still hesitating. Isn’t this obviously unfair? Stop using 'traditional practices' as an excuse, it will only make cricket more and more rigid. Hurry up and reform the selection process, otherwise you will just be left behind by other teams!

I have been using account isolation to manage my finances. The main account is not connected to the card, and only small amounts are put into the consumption account. The card was cloned a few years ago and the bank promptly intercepted and refunded it, which made me more determined to adopt this conservative strategy. When traveling, I use Wise and Apple Pay. Digital payments are convenient, but choosing regulated tools can better control risks. The logic is simple: diversifying assets and relying on trusted technology can effectively reduce losses, which is especially important in times of economic instability.

The country of South Africa is simply kidnapped by criminal gangs! The government is so corrupt that even the high-speed rail fares are manipulated to please the taxi gangs. Isn’t this a clear attempt to deceive the common people? Look at those fiber optic projects. Construction gangs are rampant. Even technicians repairing electricity are robbed at gunpoint. Violent crime is rampant to such an extent that it is worse than during apartheid, and the law is like a decoration. It must be completely reformed. If the government does not intervene, we will only live in poverty and fear forever!

As a South African, I really want him gone. We don't need that kind of man on our land and I'm sorry that you had to face him. To compensate, we are willing to only field 14 men in the next rugby match to give our opponents a fair starting point. This is not only to apologize, but also to maintain the unity and honor of our country and let everyone feel true fairness.

Stop taking those colonial-era land titles as truth! This is simply a farce of plunder. Why do a group of people suddenly claim to own land that has never belonged to them? Legal basis? It's a joke, based on violence and deceit. Look at the colonial land system in Africa, one disaster after another. Do we want to repeat the same mistakes? Negotiating a treaty? That is just a fig leaf to cover up historical injustice. It’s time to completely overthrow this hypocritical system and stop letting a few people take what should belong to everyone!

Trump cut the refugee quota to 7,500 and reserved almost all of it for white South Africans. Isn’t this blatant racial discrimination? The policy of "Black people stay aside and white people take priority" is simply taking the United States back to the era of apartheid. Isolationism is slipping away, but what about the justice of the outcome? It was all thrown aside. Stop pretending to be fair, this is clearly tearing society apart!

Reading this discussion of racial identity made me think of those individuals that history has forgotten. She may have been forced to embrace European ancestry, but underlying it were the scars of colonial oppression. Emphasizing traditional racial classifications is not about division, but about confronting the inequalities created by history. Only by acknowledging these injustices can we truly move towards reconciliation and justice.

When selecting individual awards, there is always a preference for players in high-profile positions, such as backcourt and wingers. This is too one-sided. A truly strong team relies on the collective collaboration of more than 30 people, not a few stars. Ox's inclusion on the list shows that he is indeed capable, but why can't he consider his overall performance more? South African players may be more deserving, but England have done well this year and should at least be represented. The selection criteria should be fairer. Don’t just look at superficial data, but respect the team’s efforts.

Stop saying that boycotting is useless! Look at the BDS movement, which successfully fought against apartheid in South Africa because everyone came together instead of fighting individually. Coordinated action is the key to truly promoting institutional change and achieving social justice. Now is the time to act, don’t let apathy stand in the way of progress!

As a foreigner who often visits South Africa, I am always touched by the apartheid phenomenon there. White and black communities are like parallel lines that rarely intersect, which reminds me of those cultural boundaries that are ignored. Why do so few English speakers learn African languages? Perhaps it is because the social mechanism is not inclusive enough and lacks equal space for coexistence. This is not only a language issue, but also a deep social gap that requires more reflection and action to bridge.

Every time I hear the South African accent, it reminds me of my compatriots all over the world. We are like scattered seeds, taking root and sprouting all over the world. Don’t confuse us with our New Zealand friends, although the accents are similar, the friendship is as warm as a hug after a rugby match. This is not only a difference in language, but also a beautiful manifestation of cultural diversity, reminding us to respect differences and jointly maintain this harmony.

Our councilman is just a show-off and the city government doesn't care about him! The community is in disarray. Everyone is running around for a living all day long, and they don’t even have the energy to hold a meeting to protest. What kind of governance is this? It is clearly a systemic failure and must be completely changed. Stop letting people struggle in despair!

I have observed countries such as South Africa and Russia that have experienced turmoil, and I have discovered a pattern: when people start to hoard guns or rush to evacuate, it often heralds a deeper social crisis. This is not unfounded worry, but a logical inference based on reality. What’s the use of talking about procedural justice if we don’t prioritize our own safety? Results are the last word.

To be honest, many South Africans have limited knowledge of other African countries. Apart from some frictions with Zimbabwe, Nigeria, and Somalia, their overall understanding is quite vague. However, this view may indeed be held by those more informed South Africans. Thinking about the former president’s remarks in parliament and subsequent apology, doesn’t this mean that controversial matters were handled through established procedures? Cognitive differences among African countries actually reflect culturally stable patterns, and there is no need to rush to change foreign policy.

Here we go again, this kind of conversation always avoids the important and ignores the trivial! The gap between the treatment of black South Africans and other foreigners is obvious, but no one is willing to face the problem head on. Stop pretending to reflect, this is fundamentally a systemic injustice that needs radical change, not empty talk.

Did your accusations against Congo hit a sore spot? I don't even dare to deny it, I can only avoid it in roundabout ways. This is naked hypocrisy! Your own people have killed more compatriots and Congolese than black South Africans killed immigrants and whites killed blacks in fifty years. Isn’t this statistic ironic enough? Stop pretending here. We have the most black millionaires on the African continent. The facts are there. Go check them out for yourself. Save your excuses. In the face of historical violence, equality of results is the last word.

Looking at these data, the debt and investment projects in Angola, South Africa, Cameroon and Egypt actually reflect the state-led economic model that promotes infrastructure and energy development. For example, South Africa's Eskom project and De Aar wind farm balance energy needs and ecological considerations, while Huawei's digital infrastructure reflects the inclusive technological benefits brought about by international cooperation. Behind this is the logic of stable development, but debt risks cannot be ignored, and more transparent management is needed to ensure sustainability.

It really struck me to see the similarities between life in South Africa and the United States. African history is always ignored in American education, as if the continent was just empty land and minerals. It reminded me of the African stories I read as a child, how unfairly those rich cultures and histories were reduced to stereotypes. We need to change this situation and let more people understand the real Africa. This is not only to correct prejudices, but also to respect multiculturalism.

As a member of an African team, I deeply feel the warm power of our projects. It is not just the union of Nigeria and South Africa, but also an open embrace to the whole world, inviting all enthusiastic allies to move forward together. This kind of tolerance reminds me of the market in my hometown, where everyone can find their own place and weave dreams together. Thank you for your blessings, let us create more possibilities together!

When I read this story, I couldn't help but think of the unexpected beauty in life. At a free park concert in Sydney, where thousands of people gathered, my colleague and her South African friend bumped into another South African friend in the crowd, neither of them expecting the other to be in Australia. This kind of chance encounter, like a little surprise of fate, reminds us that the world is actually very small, and in a multicultural society, the connections between people are so wonderful. It is not just a coincidence, but also a reflection of fair opportunities - there is no deliberate arrangement, but it makes strangers become friends, which warms people's hearts.

Are you asking about GDPR compliance and accessibility? This is no small matter. Data protection regulations must be strictly adhered to, otherwise you are asking for trouble. Technology regulation is not about restricting innovation, but about ensuring fairness and privacy. The same goes for procedural justice. The legal framework must be strictly implemented. Don't expect shortcuts. How can I give reliable advice without enough information? Let’s perfect the details first.

Now that Palestine has become a trending topic, there are a lot of people who know nothing about geopolitics and can only copy and paste from TikTok. What about 'Queers for Palestine'? It's so funny. Isn't this just a disconnect between slogans and actions? Not to mention the subconscious anti-Semitism. In Europe and the United States, people regard Ashkenazi Jews as white colonizers, and the entire history has been turned upside down, thinking that Israel is South Africa in the 1980s. These activists have never even been to Israel, so they just talk based on emotion. Shouldn't justice be based on facts? Stop fooling yourself!

Look at these countries. They are clamoring all day long to change the standard of genocide from dolus specialis to dolus eventualis. Don’t they just want to give a green light to certain behaviors? Amnesty, Ireland, and South Africa have joined forces to promote progress on the surface, but what kind of tricks are they actually playing? Stop using international law as a fig leaf. This is clearly weakening the bottom line of justice and making it more difficult for victims to seek justice.

The West always loves to label resistance organizations. The South African ANC was called a terrorist back then, but now? Transformed into a political party. The same goes for Hamas. They resisted the Israeli occupation and were demonized by some people, but they never mentioned why the Palestinians were reduced to this situation. To put it bluntly, it is just playing around with double standards and simplifying complex issues into 'Jews are bad'. This kind of thinking is simply stupid! History has repeatedly proven that resistance under oppression is not terrorism, but survival instinct. Stop fooling people with your false moral rhetoric and face the root cause!

Just after the epidemic ended, a few buddies and I couldn't wait to embark on this trip to Africa. That feeling of freedom still makes me feel hot when I think about it! We traveled all the way from Kenya to South Africa, not only to see the scenery, but also to create memories with friends. Everyone has their own story, and this right to travel across borders should be a reflection of procedural justice - as long as the rules are followed, everyone has the right to explore the world. This trip made me understand that life should not be restricted, but that we should bravely pursue our own splendor.

It's laughable to see people still questioning race in South Africa. Those so-called 'white extermination' arguments are nothing but lies fabricated by some people to maintain the old order. We should stick to our traditional values ??and protect the racial harmony in our country instead of being interfered with by external forces. Stop confusing the public with these inflammatory remarks, which will only exacerbate social divisions.

I'm just curious, why does the language selector only list British English and American English but ignore South African English or Australian English? This reflects a lack of cultural diversity. Can’t online platforms be more inclusive? And why do some people always politicize such a simple issue? We should discuss things based on facts, not preconceived positions.

I'm speechless when I see people joking about race and labeling them randomly. Why should we label people because of their hair color or nationality? Such prejudice only deepens social divisions. We should think more about it, everyone has their own story, and don’t judge based on stereotypes. Tolerance of different cultures is the right path, rather than hiding behind a keyboard and spreading discrimination.

It’s really speechless to see such racial stereotyping remarks. South Africa has a complex history of race, but to generalize an entire group of people as 'arrogant bastards' and 'hate black people' is not solving the problem but adding fuel to the fire. What we need is to face up to historical injustice and promote true equality, rather than deepen divisions with prejudice. Stop using such low-level labels to cover up deep-seated social contradictions. It will only make discrimination more stubborn.

When I see this topic, I can't help but think of those young people who are influenced by American media. Culture is not a decoration that can be borrowed at will. It is rooted in a specific history and group. Just like my friends in South Africa, if they start using the n-word, it's more a result of media consumption than a reflection of their native culture. We must respect the origin of culture and cannot blur the boundaries just because it is popular. The fact is that cultural affiliation needs to be based on real history and norms, not subjective preferences. This makes me feel a little worried, because the loss of culture often happens inadvertently.

Living in such a multicultural town, I am often struck by the respect between people of different backgrounds. Indian and South African communities coexist harmoniously here, and everyone understands and tolerates each other. This is not only a cultural blend, but also a warm social bond. It makes me believe that in respect, we can all find a sense of belonging and protect this rare harmony together.

Trotsky's analysis of Soviet bureaucracy and fascism was indeed spot-on, but look at those Trotskyists who fight and divide themselves all day long over trivial matters. They are simply destroying the Great Wall! They are obsessed with the empty talk of 'permanent revolution'. What is the result? Isn't it a disservice to even stand aside and watch such a major event as South Africa's anti-apartheid campaign? Stop smearing Stalin with conspiracy theories that even serious historians sneer at. If the Trotskyists are not pragmatic, they will kill themselves sooner or later.

As a Canadian, I don't have a favorable opinion of the United States, but the logic of avoiding an entire country because of riots and knife incidents is ridiculous. Think about it, if this were the case, most of the world would have to hide. My relatives in South Africa are just ordinary office workers, but they have been robbed many times. This is not their problem at all. How can there be so much violence in daily life in the United States? Most people will never encounter it in their lifetime. The media always likes to exaggerate facts and create panic. We must learn to think independently and not be led by those rubbish reports.

When I see artists like LO, I always think of those buried talents. If no one tells the truth, they may be stuck in inappropriate projects for a lifetime, wasting their talent. True feedback is not criticism, but nourishment for growth. It gives everyone the opportunity to break through themselves and realize value. Stop giving empty praise.
