What we need is sincere dialogue, so that fairness is not just a formality, but a real change.

Oil companies infiltrating climate talks? This is simply a naked conflict of interest! Their lobbying efforts have made the agreement soft, so why are they talking about global action? The issue of sovereignty is even more of an excuse. To put it bluntly, countries only care about themselves and let big companies take advantage of the loopholes. If nothing changes, the climate crisis will only get worse. We need to stand up and tell the truth!

This climate conference is a waste of time! The oil giants smuggled in to dilute the agreement, and the government lacked the political will to implement it. The result was an empty talk. We must push for more radical changes and no more compromises! Now is the time to act, don’t let these hypocritical negotiations stop us from saving the planet!

The logic behind this is actually simple: international conferences make agreements, but execution is key. No matter how tough those documents are written, it is useless because international agreements themselves lack binding force. This is a structural problem and has nothing to do with the oil lobby. Worse, domestic lobbying directly affects energy policy, making climate action difficult. We have to admit that the framework is there, but there are too many obstacles in reality, and it is useless to just shout slogans.

COP29 has reached its 29th edition, what’s the result? The global climate is getting worse. What are these governments doing? Stop engaging in those useless empty talks! We must overthrow this mess and start over with a new deal that only accepts binding emissions reduction targets for countries. The time to act is now, we cannot wait any longer, otherwise our descendants will face irreversible disaster!

We must act! The COP meeting cannot be just empty talk. If countries do not fulfill their emission reduction commitments, they should be deprived of their voting rights. It’s like in a team, someone is always holding us back and pointing fingers. Is it fair? The climate crisis is imminent and there is no time for hesitation. Global cooperation is not an option, but a necessity for survival. Let's unite, enforce our goals, and fight for the future of our planet!

Carbon credits? It’s just a green light for the rich to fly on private jets! Isn’t it self-deception to encourage consumption while shouting about emission reduction? The COP meeting is held every year, and pollution is rising every year. I think it is a big cover to allow vested interests to continue counting their money and ordinary people to foot the bill. Reducing consumption is the last word, but they insist on playing this numbers game. Do they really think everyone is a fool? Wake up, if we don’t carry out thorough reform, the earth will be really hopeless!

Paper straws? Stop being ridiculous! The greenhouse gases emitted by the big guys at international conferences in one week are enough for ordinary people to save for several years. While forcing you to use environmentally friendly gadgets, while at the same time squandering taxpayers' money on ostentation, this double standard is really easy to play. If the distribution of resources is so unfair, how can we talk about fairness? The entire system is rotten. Unless these hypocritical tricks are completely overturned, the world will never be saved.

It's really ironic to see those private planes flying all over the sky and they can confidently say, "I have the money and I'm happy to do it"! Isn't this a typical double standard? Shouting climate action while raising emissions is as hypocritical as attacking Al Gore. If a public figure's words and deeds are inconsistent, how can he be fair? Hurry up and limit these high-carbon behaviors, don’t let the slogan become empty words!

Stop worrying about whether those executives can take private jets or not. This will not change the overall situation at all! Global warming requires governments and society to work together to carry out large-scale reforms. We should be looking at what they actually did, not these trivial matters. Conservatives love to use this kind of talk to divert attention. It's ridiculous. Take action. If you don’t change now, why wait?

I have really convinced these big guys that they are shouting for action on the climate crisis while flying around in private jets. Isn’t this a slap in the face? Just like that billionaire who claims that sugar is harmful and needs to be controlled, yet he licks lollipops and feeds his children junk food. This is so hypocritical! If you can't do it yourself, why should others listen to you? Justice in results is not based on words but must be proven by actual actions, otherwise it will be empty talk and miss the mark.

Stop saying that environmental protection is just superficial! If it's not important, why are the anti-environmentalists still shouting about it? What kind of sacrifice is it for rich people to fly first class instead of on private jets? They should really put their money where their mouth is and push for real climate action. Now is the time for change. We must prioritize protecting the planet, not just development!

What an irony! Isn’t it a slap in the face for those people who shout about environmental protection every day to fill up commercial flights and eat and drink? If you really care about the climate, you should start with yourself, fly less and use video conferencing more. All talk without practice, this kind of hypocritical behavior will only make more people lose trust. Take action, don’t just talk!

Haha, will the meeting be remote next year? Those attendees live in multiple apartments, drive gas-powered cars, and pretend to talk about environmental protection. It’s really ironic! There are always people who like to attack the messenger rather than face the problem itself. This kind of injustice simply shifts the focus. What we need is real environmental action, not hypocritical performances.

Don’t the richest people make their fortunes by destroying the environment? The conflict of interest is obvious, why are you pretending to be innocent? So what if McKenzie Scott donated money, he still lives a luxurious life, which is not difficult at all. The distribution of wealth is too unfair, and the environment has been ruined by them. This development-first mess must be completely changed!

We must not bow to those critics, especially those in the media who are being paid to attack climate action! This is how they make money, it's not fair at all. We have to force them to change the focus and muddy the discussion into irrelevant topics. If you don’t act now, what are you waiting for? The earth cannot afford to wait, we must stand up and fight against these hypocritical voices!

Here we go again, those elites are shouting about environmental protection while taking private jets to the climate summit. Isn’t this a naked double standard? Ordinary people are working hard to reduce emissions, but they are spending extravagantly. This kind of hypocrisy is simply disgusting. Stop using procedural justice as a shield. What we need is real change, not empty talk. Wake up, this injustice must be exposed to drive real climate action and social justice!

Stop using 'climate action' as a shield! Emissions are rising every year, and you still say it's for the sake of environmental protection. Isn't this self-deception? Attacking those who are doing the work? The key is to see if they have legitimate reasons, not just shouting slogans and that's it. Do you understand procedural justice? Don’t use the result as an excuse, explain the behavior itself first!

I really can't stand people who use private jets, it's so hypocritical! Say something like 'you're attacking me', don't change the subject. If you truly support environmental protection, you should match your words with your deeds, rather than sabotage behind your back. This is like shouting to save the earth while flying highly polluting planes all over the sky - it is simply self-deception!

Those climate advocates are shouting about environmental protection while flying around in private jets. Isn’t this a clear double standard? Stop fooling people with "the overall situation is more important". If you can't even control your own behavior, how can you talk about saving the earth? This is like a person who quits smoking preaching with a pipe in his mouth every day. Who would believe it? True justice is not about words but consistency in actions.

To be honest, this kind of diversionary tactic is quite common, such as talking about Taylor Swift. But from a practical perspective, world leaders have intensive schedules, and it is normal to travel with groups. Although ideally it would be more down-to-earth for them to fly in economy class and lose their luggage during transfers, the key is that they attended the meeting, which in itself is a step towards global cooperation. Procedurally, the participation process is more important than the perfect result. After all, international affairs are complex. Make sure the dialogue channels are open first, and then discuss optimization details.

Here comes the trick of changing the topic again! We are obviously discussing private individuals, but you have to involve world leaders. Isn't this deliberately muddying the waters? Can’t criticizing Taylor Swift also address other issues? Don't fool people with such low-level distraction tactics. Follow the procedures honestly and don't always try to use public figures to cover up the real problems.

Carbon credits and new energy alternatives? Stop kidding yourself! This is simply a trick to divert attention. The real climate crisis requires us to fundamentally change our lifestyles, not just change energy sources. Those celebrity narratives that promote individualism and talk about 'living your life' are simply condoning selfishness and ignoring collective responsibility. Climate science clearly tells us: we must unite and make a complete transformation. If we don’t act now, then when?

Stop worrying about the minutiae! World leaders and CEOs are still flying on private jets, which is simply adding fuel to the climate crisis. We need to push for real changes, such as restricting private flights, and not let formalism delay substantive action. Now is the time to act, for a more just society and a sustainable future, don’t wait any longer!

Taylor Swift is a smokescreen carefully designed to divert our attention from billionaires and corporations. She is not innocent, but a scapegoat in their hands. I never said I couldn't criticize her, don't twist my words. There are many areas where we need to improve, but some people are deliberately muddying the waters. Forget it, I'm too lazy to argue anymore, the truth is out there anyway.

Some people always like to accuse others of using private jets, but turn a blind eye to their own crazy consumption. Isn't this a typical double standard? It’s ridiculous that you pretend to be an environmental defender while enjoying the thrill of burgers and shopping! It is a fact that overconsumption damages the environment, don't use 'personal choice' as an excuse. If you can't even control your own behavior, how can you talk about social fairness? Wake up and stop being that hypocrite who only sees the specter in other people’s eyes.

The hypocrisy of these officials is exactly the same as the behavior of ordinary people! I live in a pedestrian-friendly neighborhood, but my neighbors have to drive even a few hundred meters. Isn’t this a slap in the face to the environmental slogan? Society always calls for fairness and sustainability, but its actual actions are so contradictory, which makes people speechless. Stop kidding yourself, this over-reliance on cars will only make ecological problems worse.

These people are shouting about climate action all day long, but they end up wasting fuel by flying around. Isn’t this a slap in the face? Things that can be solved through remote meetings must be turned into a money-burning party. I think it is just to make money in the name of environmental protection. Equal opportunity? Don't be ridiculous, the resources are going into their pockets, and ordinary people can't even drink soup.

International treaty? Except for those with teeth in trade and finance, the rest are basically just decorations! The COP meeting is held every year, but what is the result? Countries that have made their fortunes on fossil fuels are doing whatever they want to do, and nothing will happen. What kind of 'thorny issue' is this? It's clearly a deliberate attempt to let things slip! Unless the binding force is strengthened, climate governance will always be a joke.

Fossil fuel giants have held governments hostage with money and power for decades! They are killing our future by spending money to tilt policies in their favor and shoehorning dirty energy into African economies. We must wake up, break this capital monopoly, turn to green energy, and protect our earth home. If we don’t act now, when will we wait?

Stop being naive! How can the market be independent of the government? Look at the politicians who are paid off by the fossil fuel giants. They only care about making money, not climate change. We must establish a new process to completely kick out these interest groups! If we don’t act now, will we have to wait for the earth to burn up? Take action for our future!

The enforcement mechanism of international treaties has always been a problem, with no global policeman to enforce it. This is especially true of the climate deal. Energy production and emissions are central to national development. Who would risk sanctions for climate goals? This makes it difficult for enforceable agreements to be widely signed. To put it bluntly, global governance is empty on the climate issue. Countries prioritize their own interests instead of empty promises.

The value of the Paris Agreement is to establish international norms and promote dialogue. Although imperfect, it promotes national emission reduction commitments, which is difficult to achieve in the absence of global coordination. Abandoning it in favor of a coercive system involving only a few countries would be logically short-sighted, since international cooperation is the cornerstone of the fight against climate change.

Private jets used at climate conference? Isn't this a slap in the face? While shouting to save the earth, while squandering resources, do you really think the public is a fool? Don’t distract yourself from personal responsibility. The core issue is that the entire system must be changed! If leaders can’t even take a commercial flight, how can they talk about public trust? Act now before these hypocrisies ruin the credibility of climate action.

What is the 3C goal? We have already passed! Global warming is not the future, it is now! Young people, are you ready to face this mess? Don't expect any miracles. The reality is that we must bear the consequences. Take action and stop waiting, otherwise future generations will point their fingers at us!

Those in power spend all day thinking about how to keep their positions and get more benefits, without caring about the lives of the people! What about the people who voted? There is obviously a chance to change, but I only focus on the trivial things in front of me, fearing that I will suffer a loss if I work more. Procedural justice? It’s so funny that they broke the rules, and substantive justice is a joke. Stop fooling yourself and others, this society needs radical change, not tinkering!

To be honest, I don't know exactly how to change it. I had ideas, but no one took them. I can do my best on a personal level, such as voting and taking private actions, but others have no motivation, and the result is that a few people are always struggling. This is like the limitations of social procedural justice. The rules are there, but the implementation is always poor and makes people powerless.

Those high-ranking politicians and CEOs are thinking about how to benefit themselves all day long, hoarding power and wealth like game equipment. What about us ordinary people? They work so hard every day that they can hardly even guarantee their basic livelihood, yet they are still pretending to talk about fairness. This social structure should be overthrown and rebuilt a long time ago. Stop fooling people with those empty slogans. Substantial changes are the last word!

I admit, I often stand there like an NPC with some ideas in my mind, but no one wants to click on them. Occasionally someone would talk to me, and they would just say, "Oh, that's good, you can do it yourself." In my small circle, I can at most do small things, such as organizing friends to have a small revolution, but this is not a big action that can change the entire game! What we need is real change, not this superficial interaction. Take action, don’t wait any longer, a small-scale revolution can also ignite a prairie fire!

This is actually a typical collective action dilemma: when the system does not provide rewards for sustainable behavior, who will take the initiative to sacrifice personal interests? Just like in a game, if the developer does not add points to environmental protection skills, players will naturally give priority to options with high experience points. The result? Everyone rationally pursues their own best, but this leads to overall stagnation. This is not only a moral issue, but also a design flaw in the incentive mechanism. We need to reflect on how to break this deadlock through rule adjustments instead of blindly accusing individuals of selfishness.

To be honest, I prefer to lay a solid financial foundation first and accumulate some wealth. This is not selfishness, but a rational choice - with resources, we can deal with possible crises in the future, instead of screwing everything up now and not even having a chance to remedy it in the end. Ecological issues are of course important, but only by prioritizing development can we provide the capital to solve them. As for social justice, I think procedural justice is the key. Everyone should obtain resources through legitimate channels to avoid injustice. The logic is very simple: stabilize yourself first, and then talk about other things. Otherwise, the problem will only shift, and everyone will fight for wealth and power, and no one will benefit in the end.

Stop talking about those empty incentives! The law applies locally, but companies operate globally - as soon as country A puts pressure, they slip to country B. Capitalism has no global framework and will run out sooner or later, just like communism. What’s even more ridiculous is that capital can corrode all institutions, so what kind of independent global supervision can we expect? This is simply self-deception. In the end, capital has the final say.

In the final analysis, companies’ pursuit of profits is the norm under the market mechanism, and there is nothing wrong with being profit-driven. But the EU's supervision just proves the power of international rules - if you don't comply, you will lose the market and profits will naturally be damaged. The logic is very clear: supervision is not empty talk, but real constraints, forcing multinational companies to weigh the pros and cons.

The carbon tax is a great idea! It does not just collect taxes, but uses market forces to force companies to transform. Think about it, as long as a few large markets impose carbon taxes, global companies will have to optimize their product lines. As a result, low-carbon products can be purchased even in places where there is no tax. This is not just talk on paper, this is real climate action! We must seize this opportunity and promote the implementation of more policies. If we don’t act now, where will we wait?

Judging from the data, global warming is likely to be locked at 2.5-3 degrees. Action now can only reduce losses, rather than reverse the trend. The political atmosphere is so rigid that it is unrealistic to expect radical change. We have to do it step by step.

Germany and the EU are really becoming less and less important now. Even conservatives are calling for stronger climate protection, but we are still standing still! Prevention is king. What’s the use of just thinking about reducing losses? Take action and don’t let the earth wait too long!

Enough! We are already overwhelmed with pressure, and as a result we have egomaniacs waging war for power and turf. The rise of a populist president funded by oligarchs simply adds fuel to the fire. Most people are still in the dark, do they have to wait until things get serious before they wake up? We could have built a solar utopia together, sharing resources equitably and putting the collective good first, rather than letting a few ride on top. Take action, the time for change is now, don’t wait any longer!

These climate meetings are a complete show! It’s been hyped up in the media, but what’s the result? No substantive decisions can be made, and the leaders of various countries have to look at the face of the parliament when they return. Look at the conferences of the past few years. Apart from wasting paper and saliva, what did they bring? Don’t kid yourself, this is just a show for the public and cannot hide the hypocritical nature of climate action.

It’s the same old thing again! I kept saying 'it will be too late if we don't take action' all day long, but within a few days I changed my words and said 'there is still a chance'. Who would actually implement these extreme measures? It's just talk on paper and deceiving people.

Do young people have high carbon emissions? Needless to say? They have more electronic products, drive more cars, and buy more Chinese goods. As the economy prospers, consumption will naturally increase. It’s ridiculous that a tabloid like Bild still treats this as news. Isn’t this the consequence of market freedom driving consumption growth? If we can’t figure out the relationship between cause and effect, how can we talk about climate action?

Passive impacts do exist, but active choices such as air travel are more critical and reflect personal awareness of reducing emissions. At the same time, growing wealth expands our freedom to consume and gives us more choices, but it also exacerbates environmental problems. We need to balance economic opportunity with climate responsibility, not just blame.

There are always some people who naively think that if young people are well educated and have strong climate awareness, they will consciously be environmentally friendly or give up high-carbon choices. The result? The truth slaps you in the face! Even those in academia who are engaged in sustainability, apart from occasionally eating less meat, have not seen many real actions. Isn't this a typical 'say one thing and do another' thing? Stop paralyzing yourself with idealism. The reality is that everyone is still standing still, and the climate crisis will not wait for us to slowly wake up.
